articles.title: अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय युवा दिवसको अवसरमा सरसफाइ कार्यक्रम सम्पन्न
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय युवा दिवसको अवसरमा रोटरी क्लब अफ गोंगबु र रोट्रयाक्ट क्लब अफ गोंगबु नर्थको संयुक्त आयोजनामा गरिएको तारकेश्वर–६ स्थित महांकाल मन्दिर क्षेत्रमा सरसफाइ कार्यक्रम सम्पन्न भएको छ ।

बुधबार बिहान ७ः३० बजेदेखि सञ्चालन गरिएको कार्यक्रममा ३५ जना रोटेरियन तथा रोट्रयाक्ट सदस्यहरूको सहभागिता रहेको थियो। सहभागीहरूले मन्दिर परिसर तथा आसपासका क्षेत्रमा सरसफाइ गर्दै फोहोर व्यवस्थापन र स्वच्छ वातावरण निर्माणसम्बन्धी जनचेतना फैलाएका छन् ।

कार्यक्रमले सार्वजनिक स्थलको स्वच्छता कायम राख्नुका साथै युवाहरूलाई सामाजिक सेवामा सक्रिय रूपमा सहभागी गराउने उद्देश्य राखेको आयोजकले जनाएको छ ।

रोटरीको Create Lasting Impact भन्ने मूल भावनाअनुसार आयोजित कार्यक्रममा सहभागीहरूले समुदायको विकास र वातावरण संरक्षणका लागि यस्ता सामाजिक अभियानलाई निरन्तरता दिनुपर्नेमा जोड दिएका छन् ।

रोटरी क्लब अफ गोंगबु र रोट्रयाक्ट क्लब अफ गोंगबु नर्थले आगामी दिनमा पनि समुदाय केन्द्रित विभिन्न सामाजिक तथा वातावरणीय कार्यक्रम सञ्चालन गर्ने जनाएको छ ।

articles.title: आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्सद्वारा कर्णालीकी छात्रा सीता शाहीलाई शैक्षिक छात्रवृत्ति प्रदान
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्स लिमिटेडले कर्णाली प्रदेशबाट काठमाडौं आई जोरपाटीस्थित चामुण्डा माध्यमिक विद्यालय कक्षा १२ मा अध्ययनरत छात्रा सीता शाहीलाई शैक्षिक छात्रवृत्ति प्रदान गरेको छ । शिक्षाको माध्यमबाट विद्यार्थीको क्षमता विकास तथा उज्ज्वल भविष्य निर्माणमा सहयोग पु¥याउने उद्देश्यले आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्सले छात्रा शीता शाहीलाई छात्रवृत्ति प्रदान गरेको हो । आफ्नो जन्मस्थान कर्णाली प्रदेश भए पनि काठमाडौंमा रही अध्ययन गर्दै आएकी शीता शाहीलाई प्रदान गरिएको यस सहयोगले उनको शैक्षिक यात्रालाई थप सहज बनाउँदै उच्च शिक्षा तथा आगामी लक्ष्यतर्फ अघि बढ्न प्रेरणा प्रदान गर्ने विश्वास फाइनान्सले लिएको छ ।

छात्रवृत्ति प्रदान गर्दै आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्सले छात्रा सीता शाहीलाई उज्ज्वल भविष्यका लागि हार्दिक बधाई तथा शुभकामना व्यक्त गरेको छ । साथै, आगामी दिनमा पनि अध्ययनमा निरन्तर मेहनत, लगनशीलता र समर्पणका साथ अघि बढ्दै उत्कृष्ट सफलता हासिल गर्न प्रोत्साहित गरेको छ ।

उक्त छात्रवृत्ति वितरण कार्यक्रमा आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्सका प्रबन्धक अच्युत पण्डित, बौद्ध शाखा प्रबन्धक अजय राज रेग्मी, बजार व्यवस्थापन प्रमुख सञ्जोक गुरुङ तथा बजार व्यवस्थापन अधिकृत सरिना श्रेष्ठ लगायत चामुण्डा माध्यमिक विद्यालयका प्रधानाध्यापक तथा शिक्षकहरू र सामाजिक अभियान्ता टेक राज शाहीको उपस्थितिमा सम्पन्न भएको थियो।

आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्स लिमिटेडले आफ्नो सामाजिक उत्तरदायित्व (CSR) अन्तर्गत शिक्षा क्षेत्रलाई प्राथमिकतामा राख्दै आर्थिक तथा सामाजिक रूपमा सहयोगको आवश्यकता भएका विद्यार्थीको शैक्षिक विकासमा योगदान पु¥याउँदै आएको छ। कम्पनीले आगामी दिनमा पनि शिक्षा, स्वास्थ्य तथा अन्य सामाजिक क्षेत्रमा आफ्नो सामाजिक उत्तरदायित्वलाई निरन्तरता दिने प्रतिबद्धता व्यक्त गरेको छ ।

articles.title: भृकुटीमण्डपमा नयाँ गाडी र बाइकको मेला, इभीमा सबैको आकर्षण
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । काठमाडौंको भृकुटीमण्डपमा मंगलबारदेखि नाइमा नेपाल मोबिलिटी एक्स्पो २०२६ सुरु भएको छ । ५५ वटा ब्रान्ड सहभागी यो एक्स्पोमा ४० भन्दा बढी नयाँ मोडलका सवारीसाधन प्रदर्शन गरिएका छन् ।

अटोप्रेमीहरूका लागि नयाँ गाडी खरिद गर्ने र नयाँ अपडेट बुझ्ने अवसर एक्स्पोले जुराएको छ । काठमाडौंको भृकुटीमण्डप अहिले नयाँ मोडलका गाडी, मोटरसाइकल र अत्याधुनिक मोबिलिटी प्रविधिले भरिएको छ । र, यो माहोलको अवसर नाइमा नेपाल मोबिलिटी एक्स्पो २०२६ ले जुटाएको हो । नेपाल अटोमोबाइल इम्पोर्टर्स एण्ड म्यानुफ्याक्चरर्स एशोसिएसन अर्थात् नाइमाले दोस्रोपटक आयोजना गरेको एक्स्पो मंगलबारदेखि सुरु भएको छ ।

नेपाल प्रहरीका महानिरीक्षक दानबहादुर कार्की र नाइमाकी अध्यक्ष ऋतुसिंह वैद्यले पानसमा बत्ती बालेर एक्स्पोको औपचारिक शुभारम्भ गरे । यसपटकको एक्स्पोमा ५५ वटा ब्राण्ड सहभागी छन् । जसमा ४० भन्दा बढी नयाँ मोडलका सवारीसाधन सार्वजनिक तथा प्रदर्शन गरिँदैछन् ।

नयाँ गाडी वा बाइक किन्ने सोचमा रहेकाहरुलाई भृकुटीमण्डपमा जारी एक्स्पो उत्कृष्ट गन्तव्य हुन सक्छ । एक्स्पोमा चारपांग्रेतर्फ हुन्डाई, टाटा, टोयोटा, महिन्द्रा, किया, निसान, बीवाईडी, एमजी, सिट्रोन, ओमोडा एन्ड जेको, डेन्जा, जिकर, लीपमोटर, वुलिङ, ग्रेट वाल मोटर्सलगायतका ब्राण्ड सहभागी छन् ।

त्यसैगरी दुईपांग्रेतर्फ बजाज, होन्डा, टीभीएस, रोयल इन्फिल्ड, केटीएम, सुजुकी, एथर, याडिया, अल्ट्राभायोलेट, सीएफ मोटो, ट्रायम्फलगायतका ब्राण्डले आफ्ना नयाँ उत्पादन प्रदर्शनीमा राखेका छन् ।

कमर्सियल भेहिकलतर्फ पनि चेरी वान्डा, केरी, डोङफेङ, स्काइवर्थलगायतका ब्राण्डका गाडीहरु एक्स्पोमा देख्न सकिन्छ । एक्स्पोको अर्को आकर्षणमा रुपमा यहाँ रहेका स्टलहरु र छुट अफर रहेको छ । ग्राहकलाई आकर्षित गर्न कम्पनीहरूले आकर्षक तथा फरक शैलीका स्टल निर्माण गरेका छन् । विभिन्न ब्राण्डले विशेष छुट र अफरसमेत सार्वजनिक गरिरहेका छन् ।

नाइमाकी अध्यक्ष ऋतु सिंह वैद्यका अनुसार नेपालको अटोमोबाइल क्षेत्र विस्तारै विद्युतीय सवारीतर्फ अघि बढिरहेको छ । विद्युतीय सवारीले हरित अर्थतन्त्र निर्माणमा योगदान पु¥याइरहेको उनको भनाइ छ । उनले नेपालमा अटो कम्पोनेन्ट उद्योगलाई प्रोत्साहन गर्न सके एसेम्बल प्लान्टको सम्भावना अझ बलियो हुने बताएकी छन् ।

एक्स्पोमा सवारीसाधनसँगै बैंक तथा वित्तीय संस्था र बीमा कम्पनीको सहभागिता छ भने विभिन्न नलेज सिरिज पनि सञ्चालन भइरहेका छन् । नाइमा नेपाल मोबिलिटी एक्स्पो साउन ३१ गतेसम्म सञ्चालन हुनेछ ।

articles.title: घण्टाकर्णका आतंक र अन्त्यको कथा गथाँमुगः पर्व
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका नेवार समुदायले मंगलवार घण्टाकर्ण अर्थात् गथाँमुगः पर्व मनाएका छन् । घण्टाकर्ण दानवको अन्त्य गरिएको स्मरणमा मनाइने यो पर्वमा तीनखुट्टे राक्षसको आकृति बनाएर साँझ आगोमा जलाउँदै भूतप्रेत, रोगव्याधि र नकारात्मक शक्ति भगाउने परम्परा छ । गथाँमुगःको अवसरमा काठमाडौं, भक्तपुर र ललितपुरमा यो पर्वको विशेष रौनक देखियो ।

प्रत्येक वर्ष श्रावण कृष्ण चतुर्दशीका दिन काठमाडौंका गल्ली, चोक र दोबाटोमा नरकट, छ्वाली र काठबाट एउटा अनौठो राक्षसी आकृति ठड्याइन्छ । त्यसका तीनवटा खुट्टा हुन्छन् । शरीर विशाल छ । अनि साँझ परेपछि त्यही आकृतिलाई टोलवासीले घिसार्दै दोबाटोसम्म पु¥याउँछन् र आगो लगाएर जलाउँछन् । काठमाडौँमा वर्सेनि देखिने यो दृश्य गथाँमुगः पर्वको हो । गथाँमुगः पर्व अहिले गैर नेवार समुदायबीच गठेमंगलको नामले परिचित भइरहेको छ । गथाँमुगः काठमाडौं उपत्यकाको नेवार समुदायको महत्वपूर्ण सांस्कृतिक पर्व हो ।

यो पर्वसँग जोडिएको एउटा सबैभन्दा चर्चित किंवदन्ति छ । जुन घण्टाकर्ण नाम गरेको अत्याचारी राक्षससँग सम्बन्धित रहेको छ । किंवदन्ती अनुसार घण्टाकर्ण यति ठूलो अत्याचारी थियो कि बाटो हिँड्ने मानिससँग जबर्जस्ती कर उठाउँथ्यो, दुःख दिन्थ्यो र समाजलाई आतंकित बनाएको थियो । धार्मिक मन्त्र वा पवित्र कुरा सुन्न उसलाई मनै पर्दैन थियो । त्यसैले यस्ता कुरा सुन्न नपरोस् भनेर उसले आफ्ना दुवै कानमा ठूला घण्टा झुन्ड्याएको थियो ।

जब उ हिड्थ्यो ती घण्टा ठूलो आवाज निकालेर बज्थे । त्यसैले उसको नाम नै घण्टाकर्ण रहन गएको विश्वास गरिन्छ । तर यो किंवदन्तिमा पनि ट्वीस्ट आउँछ । एकदिन अत्याचारी घण्टाकर्णको अन्त्य हुन्छ । एक दिन एक चतुर तान्त्रिकले घण्टाकर्णलाई छलपूर्वक दलदलमा फसाउने योजना बनाउँछन् । राक्षस दलदलमा नराम्ररी फस्छ । निस्कन नसकेपछि वर्षौंदेखि उसको आतंक सहिरहेका मानिसहरूले ढुंगा र माटो प्रहार गरेर उसको अन्त्य गरिदिन्छन् । यही सामूहिक विजयको सम्झना र खुशीयालीमा गथाँमुगः पर्व मनाउने परम्परा शुरु भएको जनविश्वास रहेको छ । त्यसैले हरेक वर्ष श्रावण कृष्ण चतुर्दशीका दिन काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका नेवार समुदायमा गथाँमुगःको बेग्लै रौनक शुरु हुन्छ । काठमाडौं होस्, भक्तपुर होस् वा ललितपु, टोलटोलमा यसको छुट्टै चहलपहल देखिन्छ । घरका ढोकामा फलामको औंठी वा अन्य सुरक्षात्मक वस्तु राख्ने, घर सफा गर्ने, चोकमा राक्षसको आकृति बनाउने तथा विभिन्न परम्परागत विधि पूरा गर्ने चलन छ । कतिपय स्थानमा बालबालिका र युवाहरू घरघरमा गएर सहयोग वा दान संकलन गर्छन् ।

कतै परम्परागत गीत, बाजागाजा र सांस्कृतिक गतिविधिले उपत्यकाको वातावरणलाई थप जीवन्त र सांस्कृतिक बनाउँछ । यो पर्व मनाउने क्रममा दिनभर तयार गरिएको घण्टाकर्णको प्रतीकात्मक आकृतिलाई साँझतिर टोलवासी मिलेर तानेर दोबाटोसम्म पु¥याउँछन् । त्यसपछि विधिपूर्वक त्यसलाई जलाइन्छ । यसरी जलाइएको घण्टाकर्णको प्रतिक पर्वको निरन्तरताको रुपमा मात्रै रहेको छैन । यसको सांकेतिक अर्थ खराब शक्तिमाथि असल शक्तिको विजयको प्रतीक पनि हो । रोगव्याधि, भूतप्रेत, अशुभ शक्ति र नकारात्मक ऊर्जा घर तथा समाजबाट टाढा जाओस् भन्ने धार्मिक विश्वास पनि यो पर्वसँग जोडिएको छ । गथाँमुगः पर्व मनाउने क्रममा काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका टोल बस्तीहरूमा यसको आफ्नै स्थानीय शैली र परम्परा भेटिन्छ ।

काठमाडौंका पुराना नेवारी टोलदेखि भक्तपुरका ऐतिहासिक बस्ती र ललितपुरका परम्परागत चोकसम्म गथाँमुगःले उपत्यकाको साझा सांस्कृतिक सम्पदालाई जिवित राखेको छ । आजको आधुनिक काठमाडौँमा इन्टरनेट, मोबाइल, सामाजिक सञ्जाल र व्यस्त जीवनशैलीबीच पनि अमूल्य निधिका रुपमा रहेका यस्ता जात्रा तथा पर्वहरुले निरन्तरता पाइरहेका छन् । त्यसैले हरेक जात्रा वा पर्वजस्तै गथाँमुगःको दिन साँझपख काठमाडौँका नेवारी वस्ती वा चोकमा घण्टाकर्णको आकृति आगोमा जलिरहेको देख्न पाइन्छ । यही कारण सयौँ वर्ष पुरानो यो परम्परा आज पनि काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका गल्ली गल्लीमा उस्तै जीवन्त छ ।

articles.title: राडारमा गंगा, भानु र प्रकाश, देउवा–प्रचण्डका स्वकीयविरुद्ध अख्तियारको अनुसन्धान
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । अख्तियार सक्रिय बनेको छ। स–साना मुद्दामा अल्झिने गरेको अख्तियार पछिल्लो समय ठूला भनिएकाहरुसम्म पुग्ने प्रयास गरिरहेको छ। रत, अख्तियारले चालेका यस्ता कदमहरु कति सफल वा असफल त्यसको लेखाजोखा छुट्टे होला तर, शंका लागेका र आरोप खेपेकामाथिको अनुसन्धान हघि बढ्दा यसको प्रभावकारितामाथिका चासोहरु बढेका छन् ।

अख्तियार दुरुपयोग अनुसन्धान आयोगले दुईजना पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्रीहरुका स्वकीय सचिव र पूर्वपरराष्ट्रमन्त्री आरजु राणा देउवाका पूर्वसहयोगीमाथि अनुसन्धान अघि बढाएको छ । अख्तियारले पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्री शेरबहादुर देउवाका स्वकिय सचिव भानु देउवा र पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्री प्रचण्डकी छोरी समेत रहेकी स्वकिय सचिव गंगा दाहालविरुद्ध अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको छ ।

यतिमात्रै नभई अख्तियारले पूर्वपरराष्ट्रमन्त्री तथा देउवा पत्नी आरजु राणा देउवाका सहयोगी समेत रहेका सुदूरपश्चिम प्रदेशसभाका सदस्य प्रकाश बहादुर देउवामाथि पनि अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको छ। जसमध्ये प्रकाश अहिले पनि अमेरिकामै रहेका छन्। प्रकाश आरजुको निकट सहयोगी रहेको बताइन्छ भने उनी २०७९ मा सम्पन्न प्रदेशसभा निर्वाचनमा कैलाली क्षेत्र नम्बर–५ (२) बाट प्रदेश सभामा निर्वाचित भएका थिए । उनी २०७९ माघमा प्रदेशको भौतिक पूर्वाधार विकास मन्त्री बनेका थिए । प्रकाश र भानु दुबै देउवाका भतिजहरु हुन्।

अनुसन्धान जारी

अख्तियारले तीनजनाविरुद्ध नै सम्पत्ति शुद्धिकरण र भ्रष्टाचारसम्बन्धि कसुरमा अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको बताइन्छ। प्रकाशविरुद्ध पूर्वमन्त्री समेत भइसकेकाले भ्रष्टाचार र सम्पत्ति शुद्धिकरण र गंगा र भानुविरुद्ध भने सम्पत्ति शुद्धिकरणको अनुसन्धान चलिरहेको अख्तियारले जनाएको छ ।

प्रकाश देउवाविरुद्धको अनुसन्धान कसरी ?

प्रकाश देउवा अहिले अमेरिकामा छन्। उपचारका लागि भन्दै अमेरिका पुगेका प्रकाश अहिलेसम्म नेपाल फर्किएका छैनन्। उनी प्रदेश सांसद समेत भएपनि लामो समय संसदमा अनुपस्थित रहँदै आएका छन्। धेरैले उनको सेवा सुविधा नै कटौति हुनुपर्ने माग गरिरहेको बेला प्रदेश संसद सचिवालयले यसबारे थप बुझ्ने काम भइरहेकोबाहेक जवाफ दिने गरेको देखिन्न। भने तलव रोक्का गर्ने प्रावधान नै नरहेको भन्ने गरेको छ। यता, अख्तियारले पनि प्रकाश अमेरिकामा भएकोबाहेक सूचना प्राप्त गर्न सकेको देखिन्न। उनीविरुद्ध अख्तियारले अनुसन्धानका निम्ति फारम भराउने गरि तयारी गरिरहेको बताइन्छ ।

भानु देउवा र गंगा दाहालविरुद्ध के हुँदैछ ?

भानु र गंगाबारे अनुसन्धान गर्न सम्पत्ति शुद्धीकरण अनुसन्धान विभागले पत्राचार गरेको अख्तियारले जनाएको छ। एकहप्ताअघि मात्रै सम्पत्ति शुद्धिकरणको पत्र प्राप्त गरेको अख्तियारको दाबी छ। योसंगै अख्तियारले विभिन्न विभागमा उनीहरुको सम्पत्ति विवरण माग गर्दै पत्राचार समेत गरिसकेको बताइएको छ। सम्पत्ति विवरण संकलनपश्चात मात्रै उनीहरुलाई सम्पत्ति सम्बन्धि फारम भराउने र बयान लिने काम थाल्ने अख्तियारको जिकिर छ । यता, अख्तियारका अधिकारीहरुले उनीहरुको बैंक विवरण र कारोबारको विवरण एकीकृत गरिरहेको समेत बताइन्छ।

केपी ओलीका स्वकियविरुद्ध पनि अनुसन्धान

अख्तियारले पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्री केपी ओलीका स्वकिय राजेश बज्राचार्यविरुद्ध अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको छ। गएको जेठ अन्तिम सातादेखि अनुसन्धान शुरु गरेको अख्तियारले के गरिरहेको छ भन्ने प्रगति विवरण सार्वजनिक रुपमा दिने गरेको छैन् ।

बज्राचार्यले अकुत सम्पत्ति आर्जन गरेको आरोपमा अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको अख्तियारले उनलाई फारम भराउनेदेखि बयान लिने काम समेत गरिसकेको बताइन्छ। बज्राचार्यले सम्पत्ति विवरण सम्बन्धी १३ पन्ने फारम भरेर अख्तियारमा बुझाइ सकेका छन् । बज्राचार्यविरुद्ध यति समूहको थामसेर्कु ट्रेकिङले दरबारमार्गस्थित नेपाल ट्रस्टको जग्गा लिजमा लैजादा अनियमितता गरेको आरोप छ। बज्राचार्यकी पत्नी रश्मि शाक्यले यति समूहबाट बालकोटस्थित रोज भिलेज हाउजिङभित्रको झण्डै चार आना जग्गामा बनेको घर घुस बापत लिएको केन्द्रीय अनुसन्धान ब्यूरो (सीआईबी)को अनुसन्धानको निष्कर्ष छ । यहि विवरण देखाउदै सीआइबीले नै अख्तियारलाई लेखि पठाएपछि अनुसन्धान अघि बढिरहेको छ । उसोतः सम्पत्ति विवरणमाथि अनुसन्धान गर्दा गैरकानुनी रूपमा आर्जन गरेको भेटिएमा आयोगले भ्रष्टाचार निवारण ऐन २०५९ अनुसार विशेष अदालतमा मुद्दा दायर गर्न सक्ने कानुनी व्यवस्था छ । अहिले आयोगले गरिरहेको अनुसन्धानको निष्कर्षपछि मात्रै अभियोजन हुने नहुने विषय टुंगो लाग्नेछ।

अख्तियारमाथि भरोसा कि प्रश्न ?

अख्तियारले गरिरहेका अनुसन्धान र अभियोजन कति प्रतिशत अदालतबाट प्रमाणित हुन्छन्? पछिल्लो समय यो प्रश्न उठिरहेको छ। अख्तियारले अभियोजनलाई कर्मकाण्डी बनाउने गरेको आरोप समेत लाग्ने गरेको छ। यस्तोमा अख्तियारले अभियोजनका लागि समय लिएपनि परिपक्क अनुसन्धान गर्नुपर्ने र अभियोजनमा समेत विशेष ध्यान दिनुपर्ने बताइन्छ। तर, अख्तियारमाथि कार्यपालिकाको हस्तक्षेपका कारण पनि अनुसन्धान प्रभावकारी हुनेमा शंका भने देखिन्छ। तर, अख्तियारले आफ्नो शाख जोगाउने र गैरकानूनी सम्पत्ति आर्जन र भ्रष्टाचार नियन्त्रणमा उल्लेख्य भूमिका खेल्नुपर्ने संवैधानिक व्यवस्थाको पालना कसरी गर्छ भन्ने प्रश्न र भरोसा कायमै देखिन्छ।

articles.title: याडियाका तीन नयाँ स्मार्ट विद्युतीय स्कुटर नेपाली बजारमा, १० हजार छुटको अफर
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । नेपालका लागि याडिया (YADEA) को आधिकारिक वितरक कुजु नेपाल प्रा. लि. ले नयाँ पुस्ताका GS70, GT70 र GTM90 विद्युतीय स्कुटरहरू नेपाली बजारमा औपचारिक रूपमा सार्वजनिक गरेको छ। आधुनिक प्रविधि, उत्कृष्ट कार्यक्षमता र नेपाली सडक अनुकूल डिजाइन गरिएका यी स्कुटरहरूले दैनिक सहरी यात्रादेखि लामो दूरीको यात्रासम्मका फरक-फरक आवश्यकता पूरा गर्ने कम्पनीको भनाइ छ।

सार्वजनिक गरिएका तीन मोडेलमध्ये GS70 लाई दैनिक सहरी यात्राका लागि किफायती विकल्पका रूपमा तयार पारिएको छ। यसमा २.१ kWh LFP ब्याट्री र २.८ kW पिक मोटर दिइएको छ, जसले एकपटकको पूर्ण चार्जमा १०५ किलोमिटरसम्मको रेन्ज प्रदान गर्छ। लामो दूरीको यात्रा गर्नेहरूका लागि GT70 उपयुक्त छ, जसमा ५.७ kWh को डुअल LFP ब्याट्री (३.६ kWh फिक्स्ड र २.१ kWh रिमुभेबल) तथा ३.७ kW पिक मोटर रहेको छ। यसले २२० किलोमिटरसम्मको रेन्ज दिन्छ भने रिमुभेबल ब्याट्रीका कारण घर वा कार्यालयमा सहजै चार्ज गर्न सकिन्छ। प्रिमियम श्रेणीको GTM90 मा ३.६ kWh लिथियम ब्याट्री र ५ kW पिक मोटर जडान गरिएको छ, जसले ८० किमि प्रतिघण्टाको उच्च गति र १५० किलोमिटरसम्मको रेन्ज दिन्छ।

प्रविधि र सुरक्षाका हिसाबले यी नयाँ स्कुटरहरू निकै आधुनिक छन्। ती सबैमा TFT स्मार्ट डिस्प्ले, ब्लुटुथ कनेक्टिभिटी, मोबाइल नेभिगेसन मिररिङ, याडिया स्मार्ट एप, कि-लेस प्रणाली र ५ जनासम्म प्रयोग गर्न मिल्ने 'फ्यामिली सेयरिङ' सुविधा उपलब्ध छ। यात्रालाई थप सुरक्षित र सहज बनाउन ट्र्याक्सन कन्ट्रोल सिस्टम (TCS), क्रुज कन्ट्रोल, हिल होल्ड, हिल डिसेन्ट कन्ट्रोल र डुअल डिस्क ब्रेकजस्ता अत्याधुनिक प्रविधि समावेश गरिएका छन्।

कम्पनीले तीनै मोडेलका ब्याट्रीमा ३ वर्ष वा ५०,००० किलोमिटरसम्मको दीर्घकालीन वारेन्टी प्रदान गरेको छ। हाल यी स्कुटरहरू देशभर रहेका २० वटा आधिकारिक याडिया डिलरशिपहरू मार्फत उपलब्ध छन्। साथै, सार्वजनिक गरिएको अवसरमा नाइमा अटो शो (NAIMA Auto Show) सम्म लागू हुने गरी कम्पनीले तीनै मोडेलमा रु. १०,००० को विशेष नगद छुट दिएको छ। ग्राहकहरूले नजिकैको शोरुममा गई टेस्ट राइड तथा फाइनान्सिङ सुविधाबारे थप जानकारी लिन सक्नेछन्।

articles.title: खल्तीबाट डिजिटल भुक्तानी गर्दा दैनिक १ लाख र बम्परमा १० लाख जित्न सकिने
articles.summary:
काठमाडौँ । आईएमई खल्ती लिमिटेडले अर्थ मन्त्रालयअन्तर्गतको आन्तरिक राजस्व विभागद्वारा सञ्चालित ‘करदाता प्रोत्साहन उपहार कार्यक्रम, २०८३’ मा आफ्ना प्रयोगकर्तालाई सहभागी गराउने भएको छ। खल्तीमार्फत रु १०० भन्दा बढीको योग्य डिजिटल भुक्तानी गर्दा ग्राहकहरू स्वतः दैनिक तथा पाक्षिक उपहार छनोटमा सहभागी हुनेछन्।

यस कार्यक्रमअन्तर्गत दैनिक एक जना विजेताले कर कट्टीपछि रु. १ लाख र प्रत्येक १५ दिनमा एक जना बम्पर विजेताले रु १० लाख प्राप्त गर्नेछन्। भुक्तानीको विवरण सुरक्षित रूपमा राजस्व विभागको प्रणालीमा पुग्ने र उपहार कुपन स्वतः सिर्जना भई खल्ती एपमै देखिने व्यवस्था मिलाइएको छ। विभागले प्रत्येक महिनाको १ र १६ गते स्वचालित प्रणालीबाट विजेता छनोट गरी एसएमएस, इमेल तथा खल्तीमार्फत जानकारी गराउनेछ।

बिलमा आधारित कारोबार प्रवर्द्धन गरी डिजिटल अर्थतन्त्र र राष्ट्रिय राजस्व प्रणालीलाई सुदृढ बनाउने लक्ष्यका साथ यो सहकार्य गरिएको आईएमई खल्तीका प्रमुख कार्यकारी अधिकृत प्रवीण रेग्मीले बताएका छन्।

articles.title: सर्वसाधारणको रकम गरिमा विकास बैंकले झ्वाम पार्दै, झ्वाम पार्ने को–को ?
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । के तपाईंको गरिमा विकास बैंकमा खाता छ ?के तपाईंले आफुले मेहेनत गरेको रकम गरिमा बिकास बैंकमा राख्नु भएको छ ? यदी छ भने तपाईंका लागि आज दुखको खबर छ । कारण हो, ग्राहकले राखेको रकम बैंकको भवन किन्दा अपचलन गरेर प्रचलित मूल्यभन्दा बढी मूल्यामा किनिएको छ । प्राविधिक मूल्याङ्कन प्रतिवेदन र प्रचलित बजार मूल्यलाई समेत लत्याउँदै बैंक व्यवस्थापनले ३५ करोड ४० लाख रुपैयाँभन्दा बढी मूल्य तिरेको छ । सर्वसाधारणले दुःख गरेर बैंकमा जम्मा गरेको निक्षेप सुरक्षित छ त?भन्ने प्रश्न पनि उठिरहेको छ ।

गरिमा विकास बैंकले काठमाडौँको बालुवाटारमा ३७ आनाभन्दा बढी जग्गा र त्यसमा बनेको घर खरिद गर्दा प्रचलित बजार मूल्य र स्वयं प्राविधिक मूल्याङ्कन प्रतिवेदनलाई समेत लत्याउँदै करिब ३५ करोड ४० लाख रुपैयाँभन्दा बढी मूल्य तिरिएको भेटिएको छ। बजार मन्दीमा रहेका बेला प्राविधिक प्रतिवेदन भन्दा दोब्बर मूल्य हालेर जग्गा र भवन किनिएको छ ।

काठमाडौंको बालुवाटारमा कित्ता नम्बर ४९ मा रहेको २ रोपनी ५ आना १ पैसा अर्थात् ३७ दशमलव २६ आना जग्गा र ४७ हजार ६ सय २१ वर्गफिटको बनेको यो आरसीसी भवन शिखर इन्स्योरेन्सका पूर्वअध्यक्ष राजेन्द्रप्रसाद श्रेष्ठको २०८२ सालमा गरिमा विकास बैंकले केन्द्रीय कार्यालय बनाउन खरिद ग¥यो ।

बैंकले यो जग्गा खरिद गर्दा प्रतिआना १ करोड ५६ लाख १४ हजार ९२२ रुपैयाँ तिरेको देखिन्छ । अर्थात २ रोपनी ५ आना १ पैसाको जग्गाको मूल्या ५८ करोड १८ लाख १२ हजार रुपैयाँ बैकलाई पर्न गयो। अब यही जग्गामा रहेको यो भवनको क्षेत्रफल ४७ हजार ६ सय २१ वर्गफिट रहेको छ ।

बैंकले यो भवनको मूल्य ३९ करोड ३१ लाख ८८ हजार रुपैयाँमा खरिद गरेको देखिन्छ । वर्गफिटमा हिसाब गर्दा पनि प्रति वर्गफिट ८ हजार २ सय ५६ रुपैयाँमा खरिद गरको छ । तपाईलाई यो खरिद मूल्य सायद सामान्य नै लाग्यो होला? यो सामान्य घरजग्गा किनबेच देखिए तापनि, प्राविधिक प्रतिवेदन र बैंकको हालेको रकम जुधाउँदा भने ठूलो अन्तर देखिन्छ ।

प्राविधिक प्रतिवेदन र बजार मूल्यको वास्तविकता

पृथक इन्जिनियरिङ कन्सल्टेन्ट्सले बैंक धितोकै लागि तयार पारेको प्राविधिक मूल्याङ्कन प्रतिवेदन अनुसार सो क्षेत्रमा जग्गाको स्थानीय बजार दर प्रतिआना ८० लाख रुपैयाँ मात्र छ। स्थानीय व्यवसायीहरूका अनुसार पनि बजारको अधिकतम मूल्य ९० लाख रुपैयाँभन्दा बढी पर्दैन।

प्राविधिक मूल्याङ्कन प्रतिवेदनमा सडकको अधिकार क्षेत्र कट्टा गरी कायम भएको १ रोपनी १३ आना ३ पैसा जग्गाको कुल बजार मूल्य १७ करोड ७० लाख ९८ हजार मात्रै कायम गरेको छ । पृथक इन्जिनियरिङ कन्सल्टेन्ट्सले कमर्सियल भ्यालु अनुसार मूल्याङ्कनको निष्कर्ष भनेको २३ करोड ८३ लाख ९९ हजार यो जग्गाको मूल्या कायम गरेको छ । फेयर मार्केट भ्यालु अनुसार मूल्याङ्कनको निष्कर्ष भनेको १७ करोड ७० लाख ९८ हजार कायम गर्यो ।

डिस्ट्रेस भ्यालु अनुसार मूल्याङ्कनको निष्कर्ष भने १४ करोड १६ लाख ७८ हजार कन्सल्टेन्ट्सले कायम गरेको छ । तर बंैकले बैंकले भने सोही जग्गालाई ५८ करोड १८ लाखभन्दा बढी भुक्तानी गर्यो। यो खेल जग्गामा मात्र रोकिएन, भवन खरिदमा पनि उस्तै अस्वाभाविक मूल्या हालियो ।

४७ हजार ६ सय २१ वर्गफिट क्षेत्रफल रहेको सो भवनको मूल्य बैंकले ३९ करोड ३१ लाख ८८ हजार रुपैयाँ तय गरेर खरिद ग¥यो। अर्थात् प्रतिवर्गफिट ८ हजार २ सय ५६ रुपैयाँ! निर्माण व्यवसायीहरूका अनुसार काठमाडौँमा अत्यन्त लक्जरियस सामग्री प्रयोग गर्दा पनि नयाँ भवन निर्माण खर्च प्रतिवर्गफिट अधिकतम ४ हजारदेखि ६ हजार रुपैयाँसम्म मात्र पुग्छ। प्रतिवर्गफिट ६ हजार नै मान्ने हो भने पनि २८ करोड ५७ लाख पर्ने भवनलाई बैंकले १० करोड ७४ लाख रुपैयाँभन्दा बढी अतिरिक्त मूल्य हालेर किनेको देखिन्छ ।

जग्गामा २४ करोड ६५ लाख र घरमा १० करोड ७४ लाख गरी कुल ३५ करोड ४० लाख रुपैयाँभन्दा बढी रकम बजार मूल्य र प्राविधिक मूल्याङ्कनभन्दा बढी मूल्य हालिएको छ । घर–जग्गा बजारमा मन्दी छाएका बेला प्रचलित भाउभन्दा निकै माथि गएर गरिएको यो निर्णयमा गरिमा विकास बैंकका सञ्चालक अनिल रेग्मी, ईश्वरीप्रसाद ढकाल र सीईओ माधवप्रसाद उपाध्याय लगायतको भूमिका देखिन्छ ।

सर्वसाधारण निक्षेपकर्ताको पसिनाको कमाईमाथि बैंकका सञ्चालक र उच्च व्यवस्थापनबाट भएको यो अस्वाभाविक खर्चले बैंकको संस्थागत सुशासन र नियमनकारी निकाय नेपाल राष्ट्र बैंकको अनुगमनमाथि ठूलो प्रश्न खडा गरेको छ।

articles.title: फोनिज काठमाडौँको आयोजनामा वृक्षरोपण तथा पदयात्रा सम्पन्न
articles.summary:
काठमाडौँ । नेपाल आदिवासी जनजाति पत्रकार महासंघ (फोनिज) काठमाडौँ जिल्ला कार्यसमितिको आयोजनामा वृक्षरोपण तथा फोनिज पदयात्रा सम्पन्न भएको छ ।

फोनिजको २७ औँ स्थापना दिवसको अवसर पारेर आज शनिवार काठमाडौँको साँखु–बज्रयोगिनी हुँदै मणिचूड दहसम्म पदयात्रा तथा विभिन्न गुम्बा तथा मन्दिर परिसरमा वृक्षरोपण गरेका हुन् । काठमाडौँ जिल्ला अन्तरगत फोनिज आवद्ध प्रतिनिधिहरू, स्थानीय जनप्रतिनिधि र विभिन्न जातिय संघसंस्थाका प्रतिनिधिहरूको उल्लेख्य सहभागितामा साँखुमा भेला भइ बज्रयोगिनी मन्दिर परिसरबाट करिव १७ किलोमिटिरको दूरीमा पदयात्रा गरेका थिए ।

पदयात्रापछि मणिचूड दहमा भएको औपचारिक कार्यक्रममा विभिन्न वक्ताहरूले धार्मिक पर्यटन प्रवद्र्धन र संरक्षणमा आदिवासी जनजातिहरूको महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका रहेको बताएका छन् । कार्यक्रममा बोल्दै शंकरापुर नगरपालिका वडा नं. ८ का अध्यक्ष पोते थिङले मणिचूड दहको महत्वबारे प्रकाश पार्दै प्रचारप्रसारको अभाव तथा राष्ट्रिय निकुञ्ज वन क्षेत्रको निश्चित मापदण्डका कारण अझै ओझेलमा परेको बताए । मणिचूड दह र त्यस क्षेत्रमा रहेका हरेक धार्मिक तथा साँस्कृतिक सम्पदाको संरक्षण र प्रवद्र्धनका साथै थप व्यवस्थापन गर्न वनसंग जोडिएको कानुनलाई परिमार्जण गर्नुपर्ने धारणा राखे ।

त्यस्तै शिवपुरी नागार्जुन राष्ट्रिय निकुञ्ज मध्यवर्ती क्षेत्र व्यवस्थापन समितिका अध्यक्ष श्यामकुमार वाइबाले निकुञ्जभित्र रहेको मणिचूड दह बौद्ध र हिन्दू दुवै धर्मालम्बीहरू पवित्र तिर्थस्थलको रूपमा मान्दै आएको बताए । विशेष गरि जनजातिजातिको बहुल्यता रहेको त्यस क्षेत्रमा बौद्ध धर्मालम्बीहरूले विभिन्न समयमा पूजापाठ, मोन्लाम लगायत साउन महिने जलयात्रा, जनैपूर्णिमा लगायत साँस्कृतिक पर्वहरू मनाउने भएकोले थप महत्व रहेको बताए । अहिले निकुञ्ज, स्थानीय तह र मन्दिर व्यवस्थापन समितिबीचको समन्वयमा व्यवस्थित बनाउने रणनीति रहेको बताए ।

कार्यक्रममा राष्ट्रि शहिद तथा शान्ति स्मारक पार्क र गोकर्ण यज्ञडोल सामुदायिक वन उपभोक्त समितिका अध्यक्ष सुर्दशन सिग्देलले वन, जंगल, जल र जमिनको संरक्षणमा जनजाति समुदायको उल्लेख्य भूमिका रहेको बताउँदै आफ्नो साँस्कृतिक पहिचान र अधिकारसँग जाडिएको क्षेत्रमा राज्यले दुःख दिन नहुने बताए । जनजाति समुदायले विशेष गरि प्रकृतिको पुजा गर्ने चाडपर्वलाई साँस्कृतिक पहिचानको रूपमा विश्वमाझ चिनाउन सफल रहेको बताउँदै राष्ट्रिय शहिद पार्क वन क्षेत्रमा समेत विभन्नि जातजातिको अस्तित्व समेट्ने गरि भिलेजग्रामको निर्माण गरिएको बताए ।

फोनिज बागमति प्रदेश समितिका महासचिव राजु नापितले फोनिजले पत्रकारितालाई आफ्नो पेसागत हकअधिकारमात्र नभएर भाषा, कला, संस्कृतिको संरक्षण र सम्वद्र्धनमा विशेष योगदान पु¥याउँदै आइरहेको बताए । फोनिज बागमति प्रदेशभित्र पत्रकारहरूलाई एकीकृत गराउँदै समुदायको पहिचान र अधिकार सुनिश्चित गराउन समेत जिल्लासमितिहरूले सक्रियतापूर्वक गतिविधि सञ्चालन गराउँदै आएको बताए ।

त्यस्तै फोनिज संघीय समितिका सचिव सुनिल महर्जनले फोनिज पदयात्राले रमाइलो मात्र नभइ अनुसन्धानका आयाम बुझ्न पाएको बताए । मणिचूडको सुन्दर ऐतिहासिक धार्मिक पर्यटकीय स्थल प्रकृतिप्रेमी र आध्यात्मिक शान्ति चाहनेहरूका लागि विशेष रहने बताउँदै पत्रकारिताको माध्यमबाट प्रचारप्रसारलाई तिब्रता दिनुपर्ने बताए । फोनिजले नेपालभित्र रहेका आदिवासी जनजाति समुदायसंग जोडिएका कला, भाषा, धर्म संस्कृति र पहिचान बोकेका विषयवस्तुहरूको अध्ययन र अनुसन्धान गरि विश्वसामु चिनाउने प्रयास गरिरहेको बताए ।

नेपाल आदिवासी जनजाति पत्रकार महासंघ (फोनिज) काठमाडौँ जिल्ला समितिका अध्यक्ष भिमबहादुर लामाले सामाजिक एकता र सद्भाव कायम उद्देश्यका साथ फोनिजको २७ औँ स्थापना दिवसलाई सार्थक पार्न पदयात्रा तथा वृक्षरोपण कार्यक्रमको आयोजना गरिएको बताए । उनले जनजाति पत्रकारहरूको पेसागत क्षमतालाई दरिलो बनाउन अध्ययन, अनुसन्धान र आलेख लेखनमा सहयोग पु¥याउने उद्देश्यले धार्मिक पर्यटकीय क्षेत्र तथा जनजाति समुदायको साँस्कृतिक तथा धार्मिक महत्व बोकेको क्षेत्र साँखु, बज्रयोगिनी र मणिचूड दहको यात्रा तय गरेको बताए । राज्य र पहुँचवाला समूहहरूबाट आदिवासी जनजातिहरूको थातथालोमा जलविद्युत गुरूयोजनाहरू सञ्चालन गर्ने, विकास निर्माण र राष्ट्रिय निकुञ्जको नाममा परिवारहरू विस्थापित बनाएको अध्यक्ष लामाले आरोप लगाए ।

फोनिज काठमाडौँ जिल्ला कार्यसमितिका सचिव रत्नमान महर्जनले सञ्चालन गरेको कार्यक्रममा नेपाल प्रहरीका पूर्व डिआइजी देउती गुरूङ, गोकर्णेश्वर नगरपालिका वडा नं. ८ का वडा सदस्य सुमन लामा, नेपाल पत्रकार महासंघ काठमाडौँ शाखा उपाध्यक्षद्वाय कमल राना मगर, कान्ति न्यौपाने, सहसचिब बिक्रम रत्न, मणिचूड मन्दिर व्यवस्थापन समितिका अध्यक्ष भिम घ्लान, नेपाल बौद्ध धर्म संरक्षण संघका महासचिव उमा गुरूङ, साँस्कृतिक युवा समूहका अध्यक्ष वेचन लामा, समाजसेवी किरण मोक्तान, सोफिया पाख्रिन लगायत अतिथि रहेका थिए । पदयात्रामा फोनिजकर्मी तथा विभिन्न संघसंस्थाका प्रतिनिधि गरि ६८ जनाको सहभागीता रहेको थियो ।

articles.title: हेटौँडामा पर्यटन वर्षको बहारः ‘शून्य फोहोर’ अभियान
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । बाग्मती प्रदेशको राजधानी हेटौँडामा पर्यटन वर्ष–२०८३ लाई लक्षित गर्दै ‘शून्य फोहोर’ अभियान सञ्चालन गरिएको छ । ‘जाऔँ हेटौंडा, रमाऔँ हेटौंडामा’ भन्ने मूल नारासहित मनाइन लागिएको पर्यटन वर्ष २०८३ को पहिलो र प्रमुख कार्यक्रमका रूपमा ‘शून्य फोहोर’ अभियान अन्तर्गत सरसफाइ थालिएको हो ।

यो वर्ष बाग्मतीको प्रादेशिक राजधानीस्थित हेटौँडा उपमहानगरपालिकाले पर्यटन वर्ष–२०८३ मनाउँदैछ । पर्यटन वर्षको कार्यक्रम अन्तर्गत सून्य फोहोर अभियान सञ्चालन गरिएको छ । यहि अभियान अन्तर्गत शनिवार हातमा कुचो र बोरा बोकेर जनप्रतिनिधि, सुरक्षाकर्मी, टोल विकास संस्थाका पदाधिकारी र स्थानीयवासी सडकमा निस्किए । हेटौँडाका सडकदेखि टोलसम्म सरसफाइ गर्दै उनीहरूले ‘शून्य फोहोर हेटौँडा’ अभियान शुरु गरेका हुन् ।

फोहोर व्यवस्थापनलाई केवल सरसफाइ अभियानका रूपमा नभई पर्यटन, वातावरण संरक्षण र नागरिक संस्कृतिसँग जोडिएको दीर्घकालीन अभियानका रूपमा अघि बढाइने योजना उपमहानगरपालिकाको छ । उपमहानगरपालिकाले ‘जाऔँ हेटौंडा, रमाऔँ हेटौंडामा’ भन्ने मूल नारासहित मनाइने पर्यटन वर्ष २०८३ को पहिलो र प्रमुख कार्यक्रमका रूपमा ‘शून्य फोहोर’ अभियान अघि सारिएको हो ।

मुख्य तथा सहायक सडक, सार्वजनिक स्थल र पर्यटकीय क्षेत्रको सरसफाइसँगै वृक्षारोपण र सौन्दर्यीकरणलाई पनि अभियानको प्राथमिकतामा राखिएको छ । टोल विकास संस्था नगर समन्वय समितिको संयोजनमा सुरु भएको अभियान नगरका ३ सय ७७ वटै टोल विकास संस्थामा सुरु गरिएको छ । पर्यटन वर्षको अवसरमा सुरु गरिएको ‘शून्य फोहोर हेटौँडा’ अभियानले नगरको स्वच्छता र सौन्दर्य कायम राख्दै हेटौँडालाई पर्यटकीय गन्तव्यका रूपमा चिनाउन सहयोग पुग्ने अपेक्षा गरिएको दाबी छ ।

पर्यटन वर्ष–२०८३ मा हेटौँडामा आन्तरिक तथा बाह्य पर्यटकको संख्या बढाउने उपमहानगरपालिकाको लक्ष्य छ । पर्यटकलाई आकर्षित गर्न नयाँ गन्तव्यको प्रचारसँगै शहरको स्वच्छता, सौन्दर्य र व्यवस्थित वातावरणलाई पनि प्राथमिकतामा राखिएको छ ।

यही उद्देश्यले सुरु गरिएको यो अभियानलाई नगरका ३ सय ७७ वटै टोलसम्म विस्तार गरिँदैछ । टोल–टोलमा सरसफाइ र फोहोर व्यवस्थापनलाई प्रभावकारी बनाउँदै हेटौँडालाई स्वच्छ, सुन्दर र पर्यटकमैत्री शहरका रूपमा विकास गर्ने र पर्यटन वर्षमा बढीभन्दा बढी पर्यटक भित्र्याउने लक्ष्य लिइएको छ ।

articles.title: इन्सेन्टिभ वितरण नहुँदा सेवा ठप्प, मर्कामा सर्वसाधारण विरामी
articles.summary:
महोत्तरी । प्रादेशिक अस्पताल जलेश्वरमा सेवा लिन आउने नागरिक अनाहकमा पिडित बन्न पुगेका छन । मेडिकल सुपिरिटेंडेन्ट, अस्पताल संचालन तथा व्यस्थापन् समिति अध्यक्ष बिचको तालमेल समस्या र भिडियो एक्सरे गर्ने स्वास्थ्यकर्मीको बाकी इन्सेन्टिभ जस्ता आन्तरिक विवादका कारण सेवाग्राहीलाई मर्का परिरहेको छ ।

प्रादेशिक अस्पताल जलेश्वरमा अस्पतालमा भिडियो एक्सरे सेवा बन्द भएपछि बिरामीहरू निजी स्वास्थ्य संस्थामा महँगो शुल्क तिरेर सेवा लिन बाध्य छन् । अस्पताल प्रशासनले प्राविधिक कारणले सेवा वन्द रहेको सूचना टॉस गरि सेवा अवरुद्ध रहेको बताएको छ । तर भित्री कुरा भने भिडियो एक्सरे गर्ने चिकित्सकलाई इन्सेन्टिभ उपलब्ध नगराइएका कारण सो सेवा विगत दुई हप्ताभन्दा बढी समयदेखि वन्द रहेको छ ।

प्रादेशिक अस्पताल जलेश्वरका निमित्त कार्यालय प्रमुख डा.रवि श्रीवास्तवले इन्सेन्टिभकै समस्याको कारणले दुईहप्ताभन्दा बढी समयदेखि भिडियो एक्सरे सेवा सुचारू हुन नसकेको स्विकारे । आर्थिक वर्ष २०८२\०८३ मा चिकित्सकहरुलाई इन्सेन्टिभ नदिएका कारण सेवा वन्द गरेको बताउदै समस्या समाधानको पहल गरिरहेको निमित्त कार्यालय प्रमुख डा.रवि श्रीवास्तवको भनाइ छ ।

प्रादेशिक अस्पताल जलेश्वरका अस्पताल सञ्चालन तथा व्यवस्थापन समितिका अध्यक्ष रोहित प्रसाद ठाकुरले पनि काम गर्ने चिकित्सकहरुलाई इन्सेन्टिभ नदिएकै कारणले सेवा अवरुद्ध भएको बताए । उनले सेवा सुचारुको पहल गरिरहेको बताउदै अस्पताल व्यवस्थापन समितिको जेठ २८ गते बसेको बैठकले इन्सेन्टिभ दिने निर्णय गरेपनि सो किन वितरण गरिएन ? आशंका छन् ।

स्वास्थ सेवा जस्तो संवेदनशील संस्थाले अस्पतालको आन्तरिक तथा प्रशासनिक समस्याकै कारण सेवा ठप्प पार्नु, आम नागरिकलाई अनाहकमा समस्या दिनु स्वभाविक रुपमा लिन सकिदैन्। तर, यसको समाधान कसरी होला? सर्वसाधारणले नै सोध्न थालेका छन् ।

articles.title: देश धान्ने क्षेत्रमै संकट, श्रमिक विदेश पठाउन बन्द !
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । वैदेशिक रोजगारीबाट आउने रेमिट्यान्सले देशको अर्थतन्त्र धान्न सहयोग पु¥याइरहेका म्यानपावर व्यवसायीले सरकारविरुद्ध दबाब बढाएका छन् । १५ बुँदे माग अघि सार्दै नेपाल वैदेशिक रोजगार व्यवसायी संघले शुक्रवारदेखि वैदेशिक रोजगारीमा श्रमिक पठाउने सम्पूर्ण प्रक्रिया बन्द गर्ने घोषणा गरेको छ । व्यवसायीहरूले नीतिगत सुधार नभएसम्म कामदार नपठाउने अडान लिएका छन् ।

नेपाल वैदेशिक रोजगार व्यवसायी संघले वैदेशिक रोजगार क्षेत्रका नीतिगत समस्या समाधान नभएको भन्दै शुक्रवारदेखि श्रमिक विदेश पठाउने कार्य पूर्ण रूपमा स्थगित गरेको छ । काठमाडौँमा पत्रकार सम्मेलन गर्दै संघले रेमिट्यान्सले मुलुकको अर्थतन्त्रमा ठूलो योगदान पु¥याए पनि सरकारले समयानुकूल नीति सुधार नगर्दा व्यवसायी र श्रमिक दुवै प्रभावित भएको जनाएको छ ।

संघले वैदेशिक रोजगार ऐन–२०६४ लाई समयसापेक्ष संशोधन, पारदर्शी लागत निर्धारण, वैज्ञानिक सेवा शुल्क, श्रमिक लक्षित गन्तव्य मुलुकको हवाई भाडा घटाउने तथा कृत्रिम अभाव अन्त्य गर्न माग गरेको छ । युरोपका नयाँ श्रम बजार, दक्षिण कोरियाको ई–सेभेन भिसा, जापानको ईएसडी कार्यक्रम सञ्चालन, महिला घरेलु कामदारका लागि नयाँ गन्तव्य खुला गर्ने र विभिन्न मुलुकमा देखिएका प्रशासनिक तथा बिचौलिया समस्या कूटनीतिक पहलमार्फत समाधान गर्नुपर्ने माग पनि अघि सारिएको छ ।

संघले मागपत्र प्रमाणीकरण र श्रम स्वीकृतिलाई पूर्ण रूपमा स्वचालित बनाउन, ५ हजारभन्दा बढी नेपाली श्रमिक रहेका मुलुकमा श्रम सहचारी तथा काउन्सिलर नियुक्त गर्न, व्यवसायीले राखेको धरौटीको ब्याज उपलब्ध गराउन र श्रमिकलाई बिना धितो सहुलियतपूर्ण कर्जा दिने व्यवस्था गर्न पनि सरकारसँग माग गरेको छ । अध्यक्ष खत्रीले विशेष परिस्थितिमा सरकारकै निर्णय कार्यान्वयन गर्दा व्यवसायीमाथि कारबाही गरिएको आरोप लगाउँदै अब नीतिगत सुधार नभएसम्म श्रमिक नपठाउने स्पष्ट चेतावनी दिएका छन् ।

संघले आफ्ना सबै माग सम्बोधन नभएसम्म शून्य समय घोषणा गर्दै वैदेशिक रोजगारीमा श्रमिक पठाउने सम्पूर्ण प्रक्रिया बन्द रहने जनाएको छ । व्यवसायीहरूको यो निर्णयले वैदेशिक रोजगारीमा जान तयारी गरिरहेका हजारौं नेपाली श्रमिक प्रत्यक्ष प्रभावित हुने देखिएको छ ।

articles.title: As crises mount, Nepal’s parliamentary committees struggle to hold the government to account
articles.summary:
On August 5, the Law, Justice and Human Rights Committee of the House of Representatives convened a meeting apparently called to discuss international concerns regarding the country’s judiciary. The core agenda centred on a joint statement issued on July 24 by three prominent global human rights organisations—Amnesty International, the International Commission of Jurists, and Human Rights Watch—claiming that the government was applying undue pressure on several Supreme Court justices to tender their resignations under the direct threat of potential impeachment proceedings.

But, rather than using these serious allegations as a starting point to conduct an independent parliamentary inquiry into potential executive interference in the judiciary, the committee spent more than four hours deliberating the motives of the watchdog groups. By the end of the lengthy session, the committee reached a controversial decision that these three international organisations should furnish clarification. The decision drew severe criticism from civil society, legal experts, and constitutional observers across the country.

A body constitutionally mandated to keep the executive in check had effectively transformed itself into a shield for the government, asking state authorities to demand answers from the international organisations that had raised concerns about state behaviour. Critics argued that the committee had completely forgotten its primary duty and chosen instead to act as a defender of the executive.

Under established parliamentary traditions, the committee possessed full authority to launch its own factual investigation, summon judicial administrators to verify whether the government had coerced Supreme Court justices.

“The fundamental purpose of a parliamentary committee is to hold state organs accountable to the people,” said Amaresh Kumar Singh, a parliamentarian from the ruling Rastriya Swatantra Party. “It is completely outside the mandate of any parliamentary committee to debate statements made by non-state actors. If an ambassador makes a public comment tomorrow, does that mean the International Relations Committee should summon the diplomat for a cross-examination?”

There are growing concerns that parliamentary committees, often described as ‘mini-parliaments,’ may be struggling to fully uphold their constitutional oversight roles. Out of 12 standing committees in the HoR, almost all are coming under public scrutiny for inaction, executive subservience, and a clear failure to address pressing public grievances.

The political arrangement of these committees further complicates their independence. While 11 committees are chaired by members of the ruling RSP, only the Public Accounts Committee is led by the main opposition Nepali Congress.

The government has registered only 12 bills in the lower house so far. Among them, merely two bills are undergoing detailed clause-by-clause discussions within committee chambers, while the remaining 10 sit idle in the parliament. As grievances multiply across the country, mini-parliaments remain remarkably silent and disengaged from citizens’ concerns.

Within the past four months, the country witnessed a cascade of critical events that directly impacted everyday citizens. Farmers across the country faced severe shortages of chemical fertilisers during the peak planting season, compounded by systemic corruption in distribution networks and a total lack of timely procurement planning. The landless squatters were forcibly evicted without proper relocation plans or social safety nets. Freedom of the press faced visible pressure when there were attempts to restrict operations at major media houses following critical reporting on the government.

Simultaneously, the self-immolation of Ganesh Nepali highlighted systemic economic neglect, while the arrests of Gen Z youth activists, including Majid Ansari, sparked public outrage regarding civil liberties, youth rights, and freedom of speech. At the southern border, citizens endured harassment due to sudden and strict customs enforcement, while everyday consumers struggled with shortages of cooking gas in urban markets. Basic administrative services ground to a halt as long queues formed at passport centres, smart driving licence distributions were suspended due to management disputes, and traffic fine structures were sharply increased without public consultation or clear legal justification.

In the economic sphere, private sector leaders voiced growing anxiety over arbitrary arrests, raids on private residences, and high-handed financial investigations that shattered investor confidence and threatened business operations across key industrial sectors. Constitutional balance suffered a setback when reports emerged that officials from the Prime Minister’s Secretariat had summoned the chief commissioner and commissioners of the Commission for the Investigation of Abuse of Authority to the Prime Minister’s Office, detaining them in discussions for nearly five hours regarding a controversial passport procurement contract. The incident raised serious questions about executive intimidation of independent constitutional watchdogs.

Furthermore, public anger mounted when the Cabinet chose to prorogue parliamentary sessions simply to issue eight ordinances, bypassing legislative debate, public accountability, and democratic scrutiny. Academic integrity was compromised when the MBS question paper at Tribhuvan University leaked on WhatsApp just five minutes after the exam began. Meanwhile, frequent failures in government digital systems disrupted essential public services, leaving ordinary citizens unable to obtain basic administrative documentation. Additionally, public resentment flared when the government reinstated personal secretarial allowances for MPs—a benefit abolished in October last year by Sushila Karki's government following the Gen Z movement.

Hari Bahadur Thapa, a journalist who has reported on parliamentary affairs for over three decades, says that parliamentary committees have lost sight of their fundamental democratic mandate. “A parliamentary committee is not merely a drafting room for legislative clauses,” Thapa told Kantipur. “It is the primary democratic forum where the questions raised on the streets, in the media, and throughout society must find formal answers.”

Thapa added that the committees are meant to hold the executive branch accountable on national security, law enforcement, public policy implementation, and administrative overreach. “Today, our committees are failing completely in this duty,” he said.

Thapa recalled how parliamentary oversight functioned in earlier decades, citing a benchmark case from September 2000. On 22 September, 2000, following a brief investigative report published in Kantipur daily concerning financial irregularities in the lease of a Lauda Air aircraft by the national flag carrier, the Public Accounts Committee convened an emergency meeting within hours to initiate a full-scale parliamentary investigation. That probe ultimately led to high-profile accountability measures.

“Contrast that historical precedent with what happened recently regarding the passport contract,” Thapa said. “When reports emerged that members of the prime minister’s private secretariat held constitutional commissioners inside the Prime Minister’s Office for five hours, the State Affairs Committee should have summoned the people concerned. Instead, there was absolute silence.”

The passivity, however, is not limited to committees led by the ruling party. The Public Accounts Committee (PAC), traditionally chaired by the main opposition party to guarantee independent financial oversight, has fared no better under the leadership of Congress lawmaker Bharat Bahadur Khadka.

Historically, the PAC was known as one of the most feared and effective oversight bodies in Nepal. It successfully investigated massive financial corruption scandals, including the controversial purchase of two wide-body airbus aircraft by Nepal Airlines Corporation, where the committee calculated specific financial losses, identified responsible officials, and formally instructed the CIAA to file criminal corruption charges against political leaders and top bureaucrats. Similarly, the committee earned national attention by launching independent investigations into multi-billion-rupee cost overruns and construction irregularities at Pokhara International Airport and Gautam Buddha International Airport in Bhairahawa.

In stark contrast, the present Public Accounts Committee has remained passive amid severe contemporary economic controversies. When widespread public complaints emerged regarding recent budget reallocations and unusual customs clearance procedures for imported electric vehicles, the committee conducted only a cursory discussion without launching a formal investigation.

Furthermore, after the national budget bill had been formally passed by Parliament and signed into law by the President, Prime Minister Balendra Shah announced via a personal Facebook post that the government would withdraw the newly enacted equity tax imposed on health and education services. This decision sparked a fierce constitutional debate over whether a prime minister could unilaterally alter statutory tax laws through social media posts without legislative approval. Yet, the PAC ignored the matter entirely.

PAC Chairman Khadka defends his committee’s performance, arguing that comparing the current committee to past investigative bodies overlooks structural political constraints. The PAC met on Tuesday after a gap of more than a month, having last convened on July 11. According to Khadka, the Tuesday meeting brought together the finance minister and finance secretary to evaluate structural damages resulting from public property fires during the Gen Z protests.

“People assume the committee is inactive simply because we are not engaging in aggressive media stunts or political brawling like in previous years,” said Khadka. “We are working quietly and methodically to settle long-pending audit accounts that remained stagnant for sixteen years. However, observers must understand our practical constraints.”

The ruling party holds an absolute majority in the committee, Khadka went on. “Out of 26 members on the Public Accounts Committee, 15 belong to the RSP,” he said. “If they choose to boycott a meeting, we cannot even meet quorum.”

Veteran journalist Thapa rejects the argument that procedural routine equates to effective parliamentary oversight. “Settling historical audit arrears is routine administrative work,” Thapa argued. “The primary duty of the Public Accounts Committee is to investigate ongoing financial irregularities and policy corruption. If parliamentary committees turn a blind eye when citizens, civil society, and the media raise urgent questions about state power, where else can the public turn for answers?”

The decline in parliamentary scrutiny is equally evident in the State Affairs and Good Governance Committee, arguably the most powerful committee in Parliament, which supervises the Prime Minister’s Office, Home Ministry, Defence Ministry, CIAA, and Election Commission.

On July 26, when violent communal tensions erupted in Sunsari district, leading to security forces opening fire and killing four citizens across two eastern districts, the committee failed to hold a single meeting. RSP lawmaker Singh, a committee member, admitted that failing to hold the executive accountable for the Sunsari fatalities represented a grave failure.

“Four citizens lost their lives to police bullets, yet the committee was nowhere to be seen,” Singh said. “Failing to summon the prime minister or the home minister was an undeniable blunder.”

Ramhari Khatiwada, a Congress lawmaker who chaired the State Affairs Committee during the previous Parliament, echoed these concerns, noting that during his tenure, he repeatedly summoned sitting prime ministers, including KP Sharma Oli and Pushpa Kamal Dahal, to appear before the committee and answer direct questions regarding state decisions.

“However, serious questions are currently being raised about the prime minister, home minister, and other executive leaders, but the committees have failed to hold them accountable,” Khatiwada said. “The HoR and its members appear to have become a mere shadow of the executive.”

Historical records show that then prime minister Oli appeared before parliamentary committees on multiple occasions, including in November 2019 to brief lawmakers on diplomatic steps following India’s publication of a new political map featuring Limpiyadhura, Kalapani, and Lipulekh, in August 2024 to discuss the Corruption Prevention Act 2002, and in October 2024 to debate revisions to the CIAA Act 1991. Similarly, former prime minister Dahal appeared before the committee in December 2023 regarding the Ncell telecommunications share deal, and in January 2024 during discussions on the Constitutional Council Bill.

Surya Kiran Gurung, former general secretary of the Parliament Secretariat, attributes the current institutional weakness to a profound lack of respect for parliamentary procedures within the ruling establishment.

“We see lawmakers reprimanding an army officer or a department director in public, while government ministers openly use aggressive rhetoric against contractors,” Gurung said. “Yet, when it comes to bringing those very ministers into committee rooms to answer for their statements, Parliament falls silent. The Speaker is the constitutional guardian of the HoR, but current circumstances show a leadership unable to enforce legislative authority. It has been more than two months since the prime minister last delivered an address to Parliament.”

Gurung added that, following major communal clashes in the Tarai-Madhesh region, the prime minister was constitutionally obligated to address the nation through the floor of the House while Parliament was in session. “Addressing these issues through external public speeches while ignoring Parliament undermines democratic norms,” he said.

The situation of other committees reveals a similar pattern of administrative routine replacing active political oversight. The International Relations and Tourism Committee under Chairperson Sumnima Udas held eleven meetings, but focused primarily on formal courtesy visits with foreign diplomats—including the Russian Ambassador on July 6, German Ambassador on May 5, and French Ambassador on April 28—rather than conducting substantive foreign policy debates.

The Finance Committee held meetings 22 times. It met on the Nepal Rastra Bank Act Amendment Bill while ignoring broader economic stagnation. The Education Committee met 13 times on forensic lab legislation while neglecting the long-delayed School Education Bill. The Industry and Commerce Committee met 13 times but ignored cooking gas shortages and market price volatility. The Infrastructure Committee met six times, ignoring highway deterioration and failing to question the infrastructure minister when he publicly threatened to break contractors’ legs during a field visit.

In response to criticisms regarding the August 5 meeting, Samikshya Baskota, chairperson of the Law, Justice and Human Rights Committee, strongly defended her committee’s jurisdiction. “As a mini-parliament, we hold full authority to gather facts and issue directions on matters within our legislative domain,” Baskota said. “We spent four hours conducting an open discussion on judicial independence. Representatives from Amnesty International, the ICJ, and Human Rights Watch were invited but declined to attend. The narrative that our committee has become an agent of the executive is completely false.”

Baskota maintained that having a ruling party majority “does not mean our decisions are dictated by the government.”

“Our duty is to enforce executive responsibility while safeguarding judicial independence based strictly on verified facts,” she said.

articles.title: Government appointments fall short on inclusion
articles.summary:
Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s 17-member council of ministers includes six women, or 35.29 percent of the cabinet. While the Khas-Arya community remains dominant, the cabinet also includes ministers from Madheshi, Janajati and Dalit communities, making the administration appear relatively inclusive at first glance.

However, appointments to constitutional and public bodies made on the recommendation of the Constitutional Council, chaired by Shah, and through cabinet decisions tell a different story. Critics say the government has fallen short of the constitutional principle of proportional inclusion, with women, Madhehis and other marginalised communities poorly represented in key appointments across the state.

The criticism goes beyond individual appointments.

Opponents say the issue is whether the government is applying the constitutional commitment to inclusion consistently when filling influential posts, rather than only when forming the Cabinet.

Public bodies such as the judiciary, Election Commission, National Planning Commission and cultural academies shape decisions that affect citizens across the country. The composition of these institutions is therefore a test of the government’s approach to representation.

The contrast between the cabinet and appointments to other bodies has emerged as a growing point of contention.

Although the presence of six women in a 17-member Cabinet and ministers from several communities offers some diversity at the executive level, critics argue that this has not translated into comparable diversity in appointments outside the cabinet.

Immediately after the government was formed on March 27, the cabinet appointed four key advisers overseeing political affairs, administration, governance and reform, and information and technology. None was a woman.

Between March 27 and August 11, the cabinet met 28 times and made more than 50 appointments. Only four women were among those appointed. Representation of Madheshis, Indigenous Janajatis and Dalits was also exceptionally weak, while the Muslim community had no representation.

The pattern was also evident in appointments recommended by the Constitutional Council.

At its May 7 meeting, the council recommended Supreme Court Justice Manoj Kumar Sharma for chief justice, bypassing the senior-most justice, Sapana Pradhan Malla. Women’s rights activists criticised the government for excluding a woman from the country’s top judicial post. After parliamentary hearings and other procedures, Sharma took office on May 19.

The three appointments to the Election Commission also failed to reflect gender and regional diversity. Man Bahadur Karki was appointed chief election commissioner, with Guru Prasad Wagle and Rajib Subba as commissioners. None of the three is a woman or Madheshi.

Other appointments were made directly by the Cabinet or through executive decisions by the prime minister and line ministers.

On April 7, the Cabinet appointed the vice-chairperson and six members of the National Planning Commission. Only one woman was included, while the appointments also lacked geographical and communal representation.

On April 15, the cabinet formed a five-member property investigation commission chaired by former justice Rajendra Kumar Bhandari, again without considering gender or community representation.

Six days later, on April 21, it formed a three-member troubled cooperatives management committee that included neither a woman nor a Madheshi.

On June 2, a four-member land issue resolution committee was established under the chairmanship of Balbhadra Bastola from Kaski. The committee had no representation from the Tarai-Madhesh region, where landlessness is most acute.

The government’s appointment record has begun to draw criticism even from lawmakers of the ruling Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP).

Speaking at a meeting of the State Affairs and Good Governance Committee on August 6, lawmaker Amresh Kumar Singh said the government had failed to uphold constitutional provisions guaranteeing proportional and inclusive representation.

“In the name of meritocracy, inclusivity and the constitution are being flouted,” Singh said, calling for a white paper on recent appointments. “Looking at the appointments made so far, it appears there are no Yadavs, Jhas, Singhs, Alams, Paswans, or Tharus left in the country.”

Singh said the exclusion of marginalised communities could not be justified in the name of merit.

“You cannot run a country by sidelining 33 percent Madheshis and 33 percent Indigenous Janajatis under the guise of meritocracy. This King Mahendra-era mindset no longer works. The constitution guarantees that the country is multi-ethnic and multi-religious,” he said.

The criticism was followed the next day by another set of appointments that drew scrutiny, this time in the cultural sector.

On August 7, the Ministry of Culture, Tourism and Civil Aviation published the names of 29 office-bearers appointed to three premier state-run academies: the Nepal Academy, the Nepal Academy of Fine Arts and the Nepal Academy of Music and Drama.

The appointments showed significant regional and communal gaps. No appointee was from Sudurpashchim province. Madhesh received no representation in the leadership and membership of the Nepal Music and Drama Academy.

Across the three academies, only two of the 29 appointees are from Madhesh, both from Siraha district, while Karnali has one representative.

The distribution prompted criticism on social media, with users questioning whether Sudurpashchim, Karnali and Madhesh provinces lacked literary and artistic figures.

Former minister Bhim Rawal wrote on social media that the appointments “bear no resemblance to the governance, justice, and fairness the RSP constantly claims to champion”.

By community, the 29 appointees comprise six Brahmin, eight Newar, nine Indigenous Janajati, two Madheshi, two Tharu, one Dalit and one Chhetri.

The appointments were finalised by the prime minister on the recommendation of a committee chaired by Culture, Tourism and Civil Aviation Minister Khadga Raj Paudel, and the decision has intensified criticism of the minister.

One recent appointment, however, was different. On August 5, Yanki Ukyab was appointed as chief executive officer of the Investment Board Nepal. This is the first time a woman has become head of the agency. Ukyab is from an indigenous community in remote Olangchungola in Taplejung district.

At the same time, critics say other appointments have not been as diverse.

Scrapping prior roles and shifting to merit

The government’s approach to public appointments has also been shaped by its decision to remove hundreds of officials appointed by previous administrations.

The government collectively relieved political appointees who had been appointed before March 26 and were serving across public bodies.

In May, it introduced the Special Provisions Relating to Removal of Public Officials Ordinance, 2026, which removed more than 1,500 officials. The government has since moved quickly to fill the vacancies created by the removals, but questions over proportional representation in the new appointments have persisted.

Government officials defend the appointments, saying they are based primarily on competitive merit rather than identity or quotas.

At a press conference, when asked by the Kantipur daily why recent appointments did not adequately reflect the constitutional principle of proportional representation, Sasmit Pokharel, minister for education and sports and government spokesperson, said the outcome reflected the results of open competition. He said that expert panels had been formed through open calls to shortlist candidates, in a process intended to minimise political interference.

“Appointments in the ministries are being conducted transparently through open competition. The application process is entirely open,” the government spokesperson said. “It was done in a way that is as inclusive as possible. However, because it relies on open calls and competition, meritocracy has taken precedence over strict inclusivity.”

Excluding appointments made to the personal secretariats of the prime minister and ministers, more than 200 positions have been filled across public bodies since the government began replacing the officials removed under the new ordinance. Yet critics say the emphasis on open competition has not addressed the structural under-representation of women and marginalised communities.

The pattern has continued in several recently constituted public bodies.

On July 2, the government appointed a chairperson and two members to the Public Procurement Review Committee without reflecting the diversity. Similarly, when the chairperson and three members of the Electricity Regulatory Commission were appointed on July 22, none was a woman, while Indigenous Janajati and Madheshi communities were also absent.

The lack of diversity is particularly stark when multiple positions in the same institution are filled at once. Critics say appointments to bodies with a chairperson and several members are often made without considering the institution’s overall composition. The scope for maintaining representative diversity is even narrower when executive positions are filled individually.

The same issue has emerged in higher education, where Prime Minister Shah, in his capacity as chancellor, has made a series of senior university appointments.

He appointed Bhola Thapa as vice-chancellor of Tribhuvan University, Kishan Datta Bhatta as vice-chancellor of Sudurpashchim University and Rajan Suwal as vice-chancellor of Mid-Western University.

On July 3, further vice-chancellorial appointments were made, with Rishi Ram Kattel appointed at Agriculture and Forestry University, Shyam Narayan Labh at Janaki University, Devendra Adhikari at Pokhara University and Sujan Babu Marhatta at Purbanchal University.

On July 15, Prof Dr Sunil Kumar Joshi and Bhim Bahadur Chand were appointed vice-chancellor and registrar, respectively, at the Shahid Dashrath Chand National Academy of Health Sciences in Geta, Kailali.

Across the seven consecutive university vice-chancellor appointments, not a single woman was selected to lead an institution.

The government also appointed former secretary Kishor Thapa as chairperson of the Tribhuvan University Service Commission and Khadga Bahadur KC as chairperson of the University Grants Commission. KC was appointed rector of Tribhuvan University during KP Sharma Oli’s premiership.

The Ministry of Education has defended the process, saying the vice-chancellors were selected through open competition on the recommendations of committees chaired by Education Minister and Pro-Chancellor Sasmit Pokharel.

The appointments have nevertheless added to the broader debate over how merit-based selection should be reconciled with Nepal’s constitutional commitment to inclusion. While the government says open competition is intended to reduce political patronage and prioritise qualifications, critics argue that a formally open process can still reproduce existing disparities if institutions do not actively consider gender, geography and social diversity in their final selections.

articles.title: How Ribdikot built a Rs460 million farming economy
articles.summary:
Bhim Bahadur Raut of ward 8 of Ribdikot Rural Municipality in Palpa returned to his village six years ago after quitting foreign employment and has since been raising buffaloes and growing vegetables.

He generates Rs500,000 to Rs700,000 in sales each season from milk and vegetables alone.

“I am more satisfied and earning more by working in my own village than I did abroad,” he said.

He is among the young farmers who have found success after returning from abroad.

Sita Kunwar, another farmer in Dabaka in ward 7 of the rural municipality, keeps four cows and two buffaloes and sells more than 50 litres of milk a day. This season alone, she generated more than Rs1 million in sales from cucumbers, tomatoes, other vegetables and milk. She has also leased additional land and expanded her farming operations to increase production.

“Vegetable farming is generating good income now because access to markets has become easier,” she said.

There are more than 1,000 farmers like Kunwar and Raut in Ribdikot.

Commercial agriculture and livestock farming are expanding across all eight wards of the rural municipality. Data show that both production and turnover have more than doubled in the past four years after the rural municipality steadily increased investment in agricultural and livestock development.

The investment made by the rural municipality has also boosted farmers’ incomes significantly.

In a single year, Ribdikot generated more than Rs460 million in income from agricultural and livestock products.

Along with increased production of vegetables, fruits, milk, meat and eggs, farmers’ incomes have risen significantly, while youths returning from abroad and women are increasingly taking up commercial farming.

Narayan Bahadur Karki, chairman of the rural municipality, said agricultural and fruit products generated more than Rs260 million in turnover in the last fiscal year, 2024-25, while livestock and poultry products generated Rs204.037 million.

Akabare chillies (red cherry peppers) alone generated Rs77.5 million, tomatoes Rs70 million, oranges Rs60 million, vegetables and climbing crops Rs30 million, and cucumbers more than Rs10 million.

Other crops, including ginger, turmeric, coffee, Myrica rubra, plums, bananas, mangoes and litchis, generated around Rs20 million.

According to Geeta Nepali, chief of the municipality’s livestock development section, milk sales alone generated Rs36.5 million across the municipality. Goat meat generated Rs11.645 million, pork Rs19.38 million, and eggs around Rs31.7 million.

The data, prepared on the basis of annual production, local consumption and exports, show that the municipality’s investment in agriculture has been effective, she said.

Kanta Adhikari, vice-chair of the rural municipality, said the turnover of agricultural and livestock products stood at Rs236 million in fiscal 2022-23. It rose to Rs310 million in 2023-24 and crossed Rs460 million in 2024-25.

Investment through groups, development of pocket areas, utilisation of fallow land and production-based subsidy programmes implemented across all eight wards have contributed to a significant increase in production, she said.

The municipality’s agriculture project has been a key foundation of this success.

With support from Heifer Project Nepal and facilitation by the Rural Economic Development Association (REDA), the project has provided farmers with subsidies for seeds, fertiliser, mulching plastic (a sheet of plastic spread over the soil around crops to keep moisture in and control weeds) cows and buffaloes, goats, shed improvements, and the construction of permanent and temporary tunnels, among other support.

Starting this fiscal year, the municipality has also launched a programme called “One Tree, Hundred Rupee Note”.

More than 32,000 fruit saplings have been planted under the programme. Farmers have also been provided with subsidised green nets to reduce damage caused by wildlife.

Commercial vegetable farming and livestock rearing have now expanded in Bhairabsthan, Deurali, Somhar, Thimure, Khasyauli, Kusumkhola, Khyaha and Falungmainadi areas of Ribdikot.

Women in Falungmainadi alone sell more than Rs10 million worth of cucumbers annually. Farmers have become more encouraged as access to markets for vegetables, fruits, milk and other products has improved.

Lila Karki, executive director of REDA, said that commercial farmers in Ribdikot are now able to earn more than Rs20,000 to Rs25,000 a month.

Kamala Pokhrel Neupane, a farmer from Khyaha, said the availability of markets for farm produce has made it easier to expand cultivation.

An organic fertiliser plant established in Kusum Khola has also helped promote organic production.

According to the municipality, investment focused on agriculture and livestock has made Ribdikot an example of a successful rural economy.

“An environment has been created for agriculture to be pursued as a business. This has increased employment in the village, helped retain young people in the area and established Ribdikot as a model local government for agricultural production,” the rural municipality said in a statement.

articles.title: Deuba set to return after five months abroad amid questions over his family’s financing
articles.summary:
Former prime minister Sher Bahadur Deuba is returning to Nepal on Thursday, five months after leaving for Singapore, with his faction of the Nepali Congress preparing a rousing welcome for him.

But his return raises more questions than it answers. Deuba left Nepal for Singapore on February 25, saying he was travelling for a medical check-up. He is now returning from Hong Kong, where he is believed to have stayed for part of his prolonged absence from Nepal. His close aide Bhanu Deuba confirmed that Deuba will arrive in Kathmandu at 12:25 pm on Thursday via Bangkok.

The circumstances of his five-month stay abroad remain largely unexplained.

It is unclear when Deuba, his wife Arzu Rana and their son Jaybir moved from Singapore to Hong Kong. The couple has not publicly disclosed details of their movements or treatment, saying only at different times that they were abroad for medical care. They have not specified what ailments they were being treated for.

More significantly, questions remain over who financed their extended stay and medical treatment. Those questions have assumed greater significance because a money-laundering investigation into the Deubas had already been launched before they left Nepal, leading to the freezing of their domestic assets and bank accounts.

Nepali citizens can obtain limited foreign currency for overseas travel and medical treatment through Nepal Rastra Bank and authorised banks, subject to approval and documentation.

However, multiple sources at the NRB said the Deuba couple did not seek central bank approval for foreign currency exchange for medical treatment, and there is no record of such requests in recent months.

“In recent months, there has been no request from the family for foreign currency exchange for foreign travel, medical treatment, religious pilgrimage, or any other purpose,” said an NRB official on condition of anonymity, citing the sensitivity of the matter. “However, Nepali citizens can also obtain foreign currency exchange through commercial banks. If they obtained it that way, the information would not necessarily be available to Nepal Rastra Bank.”

The investigation into the Deubas had begun in November last year, before the Deubas left Nepal. The Department of Money Laundering Investigation subsequently froze movable and immovable assets registered in the names of the couple, their son Jaybir Singh Deuba and some relatives. According to investigators, the freeze order remains in effect.

Nepali politicians travelling abroad for medical treatment have often drawn public attention in the past, typically under formal arrangements or state-supported provisions in the case of former prime ministers and other public office holders. The Deuba couple had also frequently travelled to Singapore for medical treatment.

After the September 2025 Gen Z protests, the Deubas flew to Singapore on October 27, also citing medical treatment. The couple had been beaten by demonstrators on September 9, the second day of the uprising, and their trip was understood to be related to medical care. They returned to Kathmandu on November 14, after 18 days.

Their latest departure, however, came shortly before the March 5 elections and was followed by a much longer stay abroad. Deuba had been ousted as Nepali Congress president through the party’s special convention in January. His party subsequently suffered a humiliating defeat in the elections, while the Rastriya Swatantra Party came to power and its senior leader Balendra Shah became prime minister.

The Deubas did not return to Nepal after the election.

It was during this period they were believed to have moved from Singapore to Hong Kong. In late April, the government recalled Nepal’s Consul General in Hong Kong, Bindeshwar Prasad Lekhak, after receiving information that he had hosted the Deubas and provided support to individuals under investigation. The couple was said to have been staying in the coastal town of Stanley. Videos of the Deubas strolling in Hong Kong have surfaced on social media from time to time, although the couple never explicitly confirmed that they were in Hong Kong.

Days after the Balendra Shah government came to power, arrest warrants had been issued against the Deubas at the request of the DoMLI.

After news of the warrants became public, Deuba said in a Facebook post on April 8 that he had not engaged in corruption.

“I learned through the media that an investigation into money laundering has been initiated against me and my family … There has been misleading and false propaganda regarding the property of me and my family. Under Nepal’s laws, while holding public office, we have submitted a true and accurate account of our assets to the concerned government authorities,” he said. “We are currently abroad for medical treatment and … the treatment process is still ongoing. The truth will come out in due course of time.”

In a bid to bring the Deubas back to Nepal, the government had even requested an Interpol Red Notice, but the global police network declined the bid. The Supreme Court subsequently annulled the arrest warrant on May 25.

The couple has maintained the same position in subsequent communications with Nepali authorities. Through email correspondence with the DoMLI and the Commission for Investigation of Abuse of Authority (CIAA), they have said only that they are abroad for medical treatment, without providing specific details.

On June 11, the Deubas emailed the DoMLI saying they were ready to return to Nepal and cooperate with the investigation, but requested that the authorities facilitate their return.

Five days later, on June 16, the CIAA served a notice at the Deubas’ Budhanilkantha residence directing Arzu Rana to appear within three days to record her statement in connection with the passport procurement case. The following day, Rana emailed the anti-graft agency saying she was abroad for medical treatment and therefore unable to appear within the stipulated deadline.

According to an official involved in the investigation, who spoke on condition of anonymity, the CIAA received Rana’s email at around 2:30 pm on June 17.

“Apart from the email, we have had no other communication with Arzu Rana through any other means,” the official said.

The ongoing money-laundering probe also involves Jaybir: a DoMLI chargesheet filed on July 16 says companies owned by Jaybir received Rs26 million from controversial businessman Deepak Bhatta, who is currently in police custody. Investigators suspect the money was proceeds of financial crimes.

Deuba, 79, is returning to Kathmandu as the legal battle over the leadership of the Nepali Congress has been reopened at the Supreme Court. On April 17, the court had recognised the Gagan Thapa faction as the official Nepali Congress, months after Thapa ousted Deuba through a special general convention. Last week, however, the Supreme Court allowed a review petition, sending the case back for a fresh hearing before a three-justice bench.

The outcome of the new hearing will determine the party’s official status.

Deuba is returning just as leaders of his faction have stepped up their challenge to Thapa. It is unclear how long Deuba will remain in Nepal. Since Arzu Rana and Jaybir have not accompanied him, Congress leaders say Deuba could return to Hong Kong.

Investigating officials from the DoMLI and the CIAA say the source of funding for the couple’s prolonged stay abroad and medical treatment will be among the questions they face once they appear before the agencies.

Leaders close to Deuba say he is returning to Nepal in line with his commitment. However, it has not yet been decided whether he will personally appear before the DoMLI to give a statement after his return. Bhanu said the matter would be discussed after his arrival. Some have claimed that Deuba plans to stay in Nepal for some time before leaving again, a claim Bhanu denied.

“Nothing has been decided about whether he will leave again or not,” he said.

articles.title: Legacy parties can no longer ignore the need for reform
articles.summary:
Three weeks after the CPN-UML and the Nepali Communist Party agreed to forge an alliance to form governments in five provinces, they remain undecided on the sharing of ministerial portfolios in the provinces where they already have governments. To increase the basket of ministerial portfolios, the two communist parties are mulling over splitting ministries in Koshi Province. This comes amid UML chair KP Sharma Oli’s push to get his yes-man as chief minister by kicking out Hikmat Karki from his own party.

Likewise, the in-house conflict within the Nepali Congress has become a never-ending game. It started long before the Gen Z protest that brought about political upheaval, yet it has not changed the working style of the grand old party. Neither side of the party seems to be in the mood to compromise, which suggests that the only motive is to remain in power. The stubbornness of Sher Bahadur Deuba in invalidating the January convention and not recognising Gagan Thapa’s leadership is the major bone of contention. However, as the commander of the party, Thapa shoulders the responsibility to create an environment to bring the dissenting side on board. This is where his leadership skills are tested. The greater the internal conflict, the weaker the party will be, making the larger mass more frustrated. Both sides must understand that their dispute has little to do with the larger public good; people know that it is largely a clash of ego and power.

If the old parties do not mend their ways, it won’t be surprising if they lose further footing in future elections. One motive for the recent coming together of the UML and the NCP could be to contest those elections under some kind of alliance, with the aspiration of performing better. However, that is not going to happen in their present fashion of working. The same applies to the Congress. Resolving its internal dispute is not merely a matter of settling who controls the party. It is also about restoring public confidence in a party that has long claimed to represent democratic values. All of these erstwhile ‘big-three’ parties’ refusal to change course could ultimately lead to their collapse. The sooner they learn this, the better.

The way the communist parties are bargaining over provincial governments and the never-ending row within the Congress suggests that they are yet to internalise why the youths stood against them last year. Party leaders’ sole motive appears to be to hold power, be it in the party or the government. They seem least bothered about serving the people in the best possible way with the platforms they already have. Moreover, the parties hold power at the provincial level and in all the local units, which offer both opportunities and responsibilities to work closely with the people. But their working style hasn’t changed. They have failed to learn despite being cornered in national politics. The March polls were a rejection of their working style, yet they appear to have taken little lesson from the verdict.

articles.title: Gandaki passed the cannabis law. The harder one comes next
articles.summary:
On July 9, the Gandaki Province Assembly did something no Nepali legislature had managed since prohibition: It unanimously passed a bill licensing cannabis cultivation for medicinal and industrial purposes. Province Chief Dilliraj Bhatta authenticated it on August 3. No licence can be issued, however, until the Provincial Government makes rules under Section 31 of the bill and the ministry issues the standards beneath them. That drafting is where this policy will actually be decided.

The architecture deserves credit. Prior consent, then infrastructure, then a licence granted only after inspection. A purchase agreement with a registered buyer anchors supply to declared demand rather than speculation, which Thailand lacked when it delisted cannabis in 2022. Section 14 makes testing mandatory before harvest. Still, four main problems remain.

Ceiling and the number behind it

Section 4(4) caps tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) at 0.3 percent by dry weight. Section 4(5) then exempts cultivation under the full direction and control of the provincial government for medicinal or research purposes. Read together, these say what the Act’s title does not: Licensed private cultivation is a hemp programme, and the only lawful route to medicinal chemotypes runs through the government itself. A plant consistently below 0.3 percent is, by definition, a cannabidiol (CBD)-dominant Type III. Much of the clinical evidence for cannabinoid medicine, including the strongest findings on chronic pain, chemotherapy-induced nausea and spasticity, rests on preparations with THC well above that threshold. Purified CBD medicines are the exception, but even they sit awkwardly with the cap: In Type III plants, THC and CBD accumulate at a roughly fixed ratio near 20:1. So a crop bred for pharmaceutically useful CBD will often cross 0.3 percent THC before it is worth extracting.

The number deserves scrutiny. Nothing about 0.3 percent derives from Nepali germplasm or growing conditions. It is an arbitrary threshold, and some countries are now adopting 1 percent. Nepal’s cannabis may exceed both, but nobody has measured them. Section 4(2) restricts cultivation to prescribed varieties and Section 4(3) allows naturally occurring plants meeting prescribed standards, yet no registry exists and the chemotype of the plants in those hills is unknown.

A threshold also implies a compliant seed. Section 4(6) defers certification to the rules, but without a breeding programme supplying locally adapted cultivars that reliably meet whatever figure is chosen, growers will import genetics or fail tests. Cannabis is dioecious and wind-pollinated, and pollen travels kilometres, so imported males will introgress into wild populations regardless of intent.

Which THC and measured how?

Section 4(4) does not say which THC it means. The living plant makes almost none of the active cannabinoid compound. It accumulates tetrahydrocannabinolic acid (THCA), an acidic precursor that is not intoxicating and does not register on an assay looking only for the neutral form. Drying and heating convert it, at 0.877 of its mass. Most jurisdictions therefore regulate total THC, delta-9-THC plus 0.877 times THCA. If Gandaki means delta-9 alone, a crop can pass in the field and exceed the limit once dried. The rules must also fix a sampling protocol, a pre-harvest window, a moisture basis and an analytical method, since gas chromatography decarboxylates during analysis and liquid chromatography does not.

Two omissions follow. Cannabinoid expression is a genotype by environment interaction, so a cultivar certified in the valley may test differently at altitude. And nothing says what happens to a crop that exceeds the limit: no retest, no remediation, no negligence threshold. One hot lot ruins a farmer, and the incentive shifts towards concealment.

Mandatory test with no laboratory behind it

Section 14(1) requires testing. Section 14(2) says the province may establish a laboratory, partner with an institution, or designate one. May, not shall, and unfunded. Nepal has no accredited cannabis testing facility, and an obligation without capacity cannot be enforced. A peer-reviewed analysis of CBD products sold online found roughly 69 percent inaccurately labelled, which is accuracy in a market that has laboratories. What does this mean for Gandaki?

Nor does anything require anyone to examine the soil. Section 3(2) lists production potential, quality, security, monitoring and food security among zoning criteria, but not contamination or water use. Cannabis is a documented hyperaccumulator of lead, cadmium and arsenic, taking them up from prior land use even where nothing is applied to the crop.

Farm is licensed, supply chain is not

There is no licence category for processing, none for testing laboratories, none for research. Chain of custody, meticulous from field to transport, ends at the buyer’s gate: no packaging or labelling standard, no limit on what may be made from the biomass, no recall requirement. The United States permitted infusion into food before potency limits and child-resistant packaging existed, and paid for it in pediatric emergency visits.

The applicant screen has the same shape. Walls, guards, surveillance, storage and a five-year lease amount to a capital test few hill smallholders will pass. Yet, nothing requires experience in cannabis or a comparable crop, evidence of working capital, or any bar on selling the license on. A grower who must hold a buyer’s agreement before consent, and may switch buyers only with the director’s approval, also has one customer and no leverage over price. The criminal record bar covers the applicant only, by self-declaration, and employees are not screened. The Steering Committee under Section 16 is wholly political, admitting experts as observers with no conflict of interest provision. Section 26 shows the cost. It permits prohibition of any variety research shows harms human health, and since all cannabis can harm some people, a power triggered by any harm reaches every variety.

Way forward

First, fix the number on evidence, then publish standards. Commission a province-wide germplasm survey with cannabinoid profiling before setting a threshold, and fund breeding and certification so compliant seed exists domestically.
