Define total THC explicitly, with a sampling protocol, pre-harvest window, moisture basis, named method and stated measurement uncertainty, and add a retest right and a remediation pathway. Set action limits for yeast and mould, heavy metals, pesticide residues, aflatoxins and residual solvents, drawing on California’s regulations. Require soil testing at application, and accredit one laboratory whose certificate gates every batch.

Second, license the rest of the chain: processing, testing laboratories and research cultivation open to universities and hospitals under ethical review, as Canada, the UK and the US do. Define permitted product forms, require a recall procedure, and extend tracking to clones.

Third, screen for competence, not only capital. Require demonstrated experience, evidence of working capital and non-transferability for a fixed term, extend background checks to employees, and set a minimum security specification. Licence cooperatives and contract-farming groups so infrastructure can be built collectively, and set minimum contract terms so growers are not price-takers to a single buyer.

Fourth, put science and surveillance in place. Constitute a statutory technical board in agronomy, analytical chemistry, pharmacology and public health, with published advice and declared interests. Train and certify inspectors, and replace Section 26 with harm minimisation. Commission a baseline cannabis use and adverse events prevalence survey before the first licence, since Nepal’s only figures come from small, convenience samples of psychiatric outpatients and undergraduates.

None of this resolves the question underneath. The 1976 Act permits special licences to the Government of Nepal or an institution under its full supervision, not to a province, and Section 22(2) concedes as much by referring unlicensed cultivation back to federal narcotics law. Section 17(c) directs the Steering Committee to encourage processing of the harvest into medicines and consumer products, which is where the value and the jobs are, but Section 29 defers export to a federal framework that offers no pathway. Gandaki can licence a crop it cannot legally sell abroad, so the economic case rests on a decision Kathmandu has not taken. Amend the 1976 Act to create a carve-out and open a clear route. Until then, the person carrying the legal risk is a farmer standing in a field.

A threshold can be written in an afternoon; a laboratory takes years; a baseline can be measured only once; and a swamped landrace does not come back. The Act was the easy part.

articles.title: What’s in a surname?
articles.summary:
Imagine an invisibility cloak that follows a woman wherever she goes. It hides the right half of her body and makes it transparent. A man stands behind her, making her body appear half hers and half his. Nobody finds it strange because people believe that a woman’s identity is inextricably linked to the men in her life. An invisibility cloak sounds mystical, something that can only appear in fantasy movies. But if you look more closely, a woman has walked around with it since her birth. It is her surname.

“I will be removing the surname from my citizenship card when I grow up”, I declared while cleaning the dining table when I was very young. My mom turned around from the kitchen stove and gave me a furious look. My father, who was quietly using his phone at the dining table, chuckled without lifting or turning his head. “This girl’s reading habit has gone too far now”, said my mother, as she thought I got such ideas from the fictional novels I read. The kitchen went silent; I giggled. “This is not something to joke about, naani. Don’t try to be oversmart,” she added.

That moment ended; days and nights went by, but even today, I ponder why it was my mother who was greatly offended by me not wanting to keep my father’s and my to-be husband’s surname. Why didn’t my father react in the same way? Is it because my mother knows that the system and society will recognise me, her and any other woman only by a man’s surname?

But it isn’t just my mother who stands in the way of me finding my identity outside the surname I’m given. The whole historical idea of Manuvaadi gotra, as well as today’s governmental system, will not recognise me as a citizen without a proper lineage or just my mother’s name. But why would I entertain a surname and gotra that is one ‘donation’ (kanyadaan) away from changing? Why wouldn’t I leave the section on my citizenship empty, if I, as a woman—without help from a man—possess no title to fill in it?

Systems that failed her

Traditions differ from place to place. Different rituals exist around the world. However, when it comes to giving surnames to women, the practice remains universal. They are given either their father’s or their husband’s surname. Most people find this practice normal because this concept isn’t new; it has been driving along with humanity for centuries. Even when there are no binding roles, most women—in a heterosexual marriage—still prefer to take their husband’s surname. Moreover, research shows that women need to use their full name in a professional setting to gain recognition in a male-dominated field, especially STEM. Her name alone doesn’t suffice because she will be disregarded as a woman and automatically be confused as a man. Thus, this indicates that women still have a long fight against patriarchal norms.

In a heterosexual marriage, it takes a man and a woman to continue a lineage. But the woman is deemed dispensable while creating vamsavalis. Her existence remains questionable when a genealogical paper is checked. Even when she carries the weight of her surname, she has no identity. Where will she be recognised, and when will her name be enough? The Constitution of Nepal, 2015, grants citizenship rights to children in their mother’s name. But this provision has yet to be realised in practice. The process of obtaining citizenship through a mother’s name is filled with obstacles. We hear many stories about the lengthy bureaucratic processes, filled with questions and suspicions, when people go to have their citizenship cards made in their mother’s name. In some cases, children have been denied their citizenship altogether. Her name, although clung to a man’s label, isn’t sufficient to provide her child with a better future.

Even when a woman holds a man’s surname, her name is disposable and insignificant. The prevailing social and governmental systems fail her. Her surname fails her. She drags her last name around with pride, but it doesn’t give her the same honour. She remains in the shadows of men forever.

Where do women belong?

Another incident transpired. Every Dashain, on Dashami, our ‘clan’ has a kuldevata puja. Everyone in my family, except me, is ‘eligible’ to participate in it. I asked my mother why I was the outlier in this ritual, and she said that it was because my gotra would change after I got married. This ritual indirectly states that I will eventually be tossed away like a foster pet to my ‘in-laws’ to claim their gotra and surname. That is why I don’t qualify to get involved in the ‘clan’ I was born in. The women in my family believe that if I mistakenly hear the name of the kuldevata and their mantra, I will become a curse for the whole family.

So, questions arise: “Will my to-be husband’s family name make me the daughter of their lineage when the surname I held since birth couldn’t make me my family’s own?” Where do I belong? Where is my and every woman’s sole identity? Will I and they always just remain “falaano surname ko chhori” and “falaano surname ko budhi?” What is so good about keeping a surname that fails to give me a home?

Hence, as a woman, I would claim that everything I achieve belongs to my first name. As a woman, I would bend Shakespeare’s saying and instead ask: “What’s in a surname?”

articles.title: No more shelving of study commission reports
articles.summary:
Over a dozen commissions and committees have been formed in Nepal in the span of three decades, and largely none of their recommendations has been implemented. This tells the story of how successive governments over the decades constituted high-level panels to probe corruption, atrocities committed during different movements, the grabbing of public land and smuggling, among other issues, only to shelve their reports after they are submitted. In several instances, governments have not even received the reports from these panels.

The unresponsive attitude of successive governments has remained largely unchanged since the 1990s. In May 1990, the interim government led by Krishna Prasad Bhattarai formed a commission under the chairmanship of Janardan Mallik to investigate the loss of life and property and human rights abuses during the People’s Movement. Yet governments that came to power on the sacrifices of dozens of people who fought for democracy took little meaningful action.

The same attitude was repeated after the 2006 People’s Movement. The report of the Krishna Jung Rayamajhi Commission, formed to investigate the suppression of the movement, continues to gather dust, with successive governments showing little interest in implementing its recommendations. There are several other instances in which the Nepali Congress, the CPN-UML and the erstwhile CPN (Maoist Centre) have dumped the reports prepared after extensive study.

The incumbent government is also treading the same path. Ten panels have either been constituted under the Balendra Shah administration or have had their reports come to rest on its shoulders for implementation. Yet none of their recommendations has been fully implemented. The implementation of the Gauri Bahadur Karki commission’s report on state atrocities during the Gen Z movement has so far resulted in the arrest of former prime minister and CPN-UML chair KP Sharma Oli and former home minister Ramesh Lekhak. No progress has been made in implementing the National Human Rights Commission’s recommendations concerning human rights violations during the September 8 and 9 protests, to name just a few.

As Mallik aptly observed, governments have long used such panels to diffuse public outrage and ease political pressure, only to let their reports collect cobwebs once the immediate crisis has passed. The pattern has persisted, regardless of the political transformations the country has undergone over the years.

This is a treacherous betrayal of the people waiting for justice and of the wider public that expects meaningful change based on the findings of such commissions. These investigations often take months and consume considerable state resources, only for their findings to be ignored. Hence, ignorance also amounts to a waste of public resources. Failure to act on their recommendations not only disrespects the experts who served on these panels but also undermines the credibility of the investigative process itself.

More importantly, inaction allows wrongdoing to be repeated with little fear of accountability, deepening the culture of impunity. Had those named by the Mallik Commission been held accountable, those in power in 2006 might have thought twice before using indiscriminate force against peaceful protesters. The same lesson applies to the Gen Z movement.

It is not too late for the Shah government to act. Its commitments to ending impunity and delivering justice will ring hollow if it, too, chooses to shelve commission reports rather than act on their findings.

articles.title: In ‘One foot in front of the other’, four runners build their utopia on the road
articles.summary:
Few things help people bond more than being in the trenches through an extreme experience: travelling/living with someone over a long period, being on an outdoor schedule, working in the same department overseen by a tyrant, or taking part in high-endurance sports like trekking or long-distance running.

It is during adverse conditions that all politeness flies out of the window, and people show you who they really are. It’s intimacy unlike anything else. It’s what probably explains the thick camaraderie at the heart of Basav Biradar’s 62-minute documentary, One Foot in Front of The Other.

Here, Biradar chronicles a 2018 run between Bengaluru to Chennai, along with backstories of the four runners: Santosh, Chandra, Mani and Krishan. As the group undertakes the journey of 340-odd kms, the film gradually bleeds the noise around long-distance running as an endurance sport.

Santosh, a US-returned software techie (one might consider him a Bengaluru cliche), took up social work on the side in the mid 2000s. Dissatisfied with how it wasn’t leading to any ‘positive’ change, he started a running group in the late 2000s, inviting friends, acquaintances and strangers to join him.

With Runner’s High, Santosh found an outlet for his compassion to do good for society, while also seeing tangible results for his effort. Santosh leads the group over four and a half days, meticulously planning each stop, the food to be had, the overall pace of the group, ensuring everyone’s safety (especially Chandra, the only female runner here).

Biradar’s film is a pared-down project, with the rawness of a V-log. If the role of a documentarian is to become invisible around their subjects, Biradar is successful. None of the runners seem conscious of the camera, and keep their banter going. It seems like the filmmaker has spent enough time with the ‘characters’ here, so as to never treat presence as an invasion of their privacy. More than once, during the film, the runners warmly greet the camera.

All four runners hail from different backgrounds – Krishan recounts growing up during the 1980s insurgency in Punjab. Having moved to Bengaluru in 1998, he began training under Santosh from the late 2000s. Chandra, originally hailing from Kerala, discovered her passion for long-distance running at the Mumbai marathon at the age of 45, when she accidentally won in her category.

At the age of 60, she’s the eldest and among the most resilient in the group. Mani, a native of Trichy (Tamil Nadu), seems to look at running as a way to test himself, but confesses that it’s the feeling of community that has brought him back to Runner’s High again and again.

As much as high-endurance sports are about the myth of discipline, focus and isolation – a thing I appreciated about Santosh in the film is his intent to bust all of it. He calls his group of long-distance runners, JLBR: Jobless Lazy Boring Runners.

“Anyone can do it, as long as they have the time,” Santosh tells the camera, which is, of course, not entirely true.

During the run, everyone’s mindful about doing their best, and inspiring each other to keep moving when things become unpleasant beyond a certain degree. None of the runners want to be the one to slow down the entire group. And yet, at no point, are any of the runners being forced to finish the run at the expense of their mental or physical health. An unspoken trust binds the group.

The group’s culture, primarily under Santosh’s leadership, is a Utopian bubble unto itself. Everyone tries their best, they wait for the one struggling on a particular day, and manage to inspire each other to get over the finish line.

As a result, long-distance running becomes a metaphor for life, and the generosity on the road begins to feel like a larger philosophy for one’s way of living. I think running for such hours over long distances gives one time to think: about their value system, beliefs. I’d like to believe after all the pain a body is subjected to, it turns one into a humble, empathetic version of themselves.

One thing I particularly enjoyed about Biradar’s documentary was the idealism he brought out, especially in this world of late-stage capitalism. I associated its sincerity and charm with the Doordarshan films I grew up watching. I was reminded of a film that I’d caught by chance, Parvati Menon’s Triyatri (1990).

Menon’s film follows three teenage boys, who have just got their results for 10th boards. They’re encouraged to learn from living, by riding their bicycles from Bombay to Kanyakumari (by none other than Utpal Dutt, who plays a character’s grandfather here). Menon’s film has a sense of wading into the unknown, and the optimistic outlook to treat any adverse experience as an opportunity to build character. Similarly, as much as there’s toil, sweat and pain in the mission at the heart of Biradar’s film, there’s also a sense of exploration.

While Santosh, Chandra, Mani and Krishan put their bodies on the line, by running on an average for 11 hours on consecutive days (about 70 kms per day), they also never seem to be trying to make it look aspirational. Biradar’s film, while recording this extraordinary feat, never frames the runners as anything beyond ordinary people.

It might make viewers think of taking up long-distance running as a hobby (it’s obviously harder than the film makes it look). However, as the film’s name also accurately explains, it’s only about putting one foot in front of the other.

articles.title: Mental wellbeing: The ideal self we were taught to dream of
articles.summary:
A few weeks ago, while occupied with the ordinary routines of daily life, a random thought came to me: What would my ideal self look like? What would I consider a successful life?

As I genuinely reflected on the question, I noticed a pattern emerging. The first images that came to mind were surprisingly concrete and material: a particular physical appearance, a certain car, a beautiful apartment, financial security, perhaps a lifestyle that would signal that I had ‘made it’.

I found myself amused and slightly unsettled by the realisation that the first things I associated with my ideal self were material possessions and outward appearances. It made me wonder: Where did I learn to define success this way? Why do these things feel like evidence of becoming the person I am supposed to be?

The more I thought about it, the more I recognised that perhaps these desires did not originate entirely from within me. They may have been shaped, gradually and almost imperceptibly, by the world around me.

A particular scene from Little Miss Sunshine, a movie I find beautiful, came to mind. Little Olive is travelling across the country with her family to attend a children's beauty pageant. She is excited about the trip and has been looking forward to the competition for a long time, even practising the dance routine she plans to perform with her grandfather.

At one point, the family stops at a diner for breakfast. Olive excitedly orders a ‘waffle à la mode’, a waffle topped with vanilla ice cream. Her father, Richard, immediately intervenes. Rather than openly insulting her, he uses an insidious, passive-aggressive logic. He tells Olive that the women who compete in the Miss America pageant are always skinny, and that eating ice cream makes people fat.

I remember feeling infuriated watching that scene. There is something particularly disturbing about hearing an adult speak to a little girl that way, not simply because of what he says, but because of what he introduces into her world.

Before that moment, Olive is completely innocent of the idea that her body needs to be evaluated. She is excited about her waffle, her dance, and her pageant. Her body is simply her body; it is not yet a problem she needs to solve.

And then, almost instantaneously, that changes.

Olive becomes visibly self-conscious, absorbing the implication behind her father's words: perhaps there is something wrong with the way she is. Perhaps she needs to become different in order to be accepted.

That moment stayed with me because I think it captures something much larger about how we learn to see ourselves.

The message rarely arrives as an explicit instruction saying, “You must look this way to be worthy.” Instead, it comes in fragments, in advertisements, movies, social media, conversations, family expectations, compliments, jokes, fashion, and the lifestyles presented to us as desirable.

Over time, these messages become so familiar that they no longer feel external. They begin to sound like our own thoughts.

We learn that certain bodies are more desirable, certain careers more respectable, certain homes more successful, and certain cars more prestigious. We learn that having more money means achieving more, that attractiveness determines worth, and that productivity is a measure of value. Most importantly, these standards are rarely presented as standards. They are presented as normal.

This is what made my original question about my ‘ideal self’ feel so revealing.

When I first imagined the person I wanted to become, I instinctively imagined the visible markers of success: how I would look, what I would drive, where I would live, and how much money I would have. None of these desires are inherently wrong.

But I began to wonder whether these things were actually my definition of a meaningful life, or whether I had simply learned to associate them with one.

Perhaps the more important question is not “what would my ideal self have?” but “who would my ideal self be?”

Would I be kinder? More courageous? More emotionally grounded? Would I have meaningful relationships? Would I be someone who makes others feel safe and accepted? Would I have the freedom to spend my time in ways that feel meaningful? Would I be curious, compassionate, resilient, generous, or intellectually fulfilled?

And perhaps most importantly, would I be able to exist without constantly feeling that I needed to become someone else before I was allowed to feel enough?

As adults, the messages become more sophisticated, but the underlying lesson remains remarkably similar: there is a version of you that is more acceptable than the person you are right now.

And so, we spend much of our lives moving toward an imagined version of ourselves, sometimes without stopping to ask who created that image in the first place. Perhaps introspection allows us to separate these two voices: the voice of what we genuinely want, and the voice of what we have been taught to want.

The answer is not to reject material things or ambition altogether. The problem is not wanting a beautiful apartment, financial stability, or a particular appearance. The problem begins when these things become conditions for self-worth, when they stop being things we enjoy having and become evidence that we are finally enough.

The ideal self does not need to be the person who has everything society has taught us to want. Rather, it can be the person who is more conscious of why they want what they want.

Someone who can recognise the standards we have inherited without automatically accepting them. Someone who can enjoy beauty without believing that beauty determines worth. Someone who can pursue success without allowing success to determine their value. Someone who can want more for themselves without believing that who they are now is somehow inadequate.

Perhaps this is a more meaningful definition of the ideal self: not a perfected version of ourselves, but a more authentic one.

And, in the end, an ideal life is not about finally becoming the person who fits the picture perfectly. It is about becoming comfortable enough with ourselves to ask whether we even want to be in the picture.

articles.title: Numa Sambahamphe on the shows and channels she keeps coming back to
articles.summary:
Two twins Qwon & Qjin vlog about fashion, lifestyle, decor, travelling, cooking, learning new skills, and everyday life. They are one of my go to comfort shows to watch. Whenever I feel down or tired or am just resting at home, I go watch them all the time.

The Try Guys are a fun group who basically try everything from games, makeup, cooking, challenges, and even things they’ve never done before. They approach everything like complete beginners. I have been watching them since 2020 and still enjoy everything they put out.

Running Man

It’s a Korean variety show and definitely one of my all-time favourites. I love how chaotic, funny, and unpredictable every episode is, with the cast competing in different games and challenges while constantly making fun of each other. It’s one of those shows I can watch anytime.

One of those shows I’d recommend if you’re into sci-fi, adventure, and a little bit of everything. I love how imaginative the stories are, with time travel, different worlds, strange creatures, and completely unexpected adventures.

The Big Bang Theory

When I am looking for a fun geeky sitcom with a mix of comedy, friendship, and everyday chaos, ‘The Big Bang Theory’ is my ultimate choice. I love the dynamic between the characters and how their completely different personalities somehow work so well together.

One Piece is not just an anime to me; it’s a story that reflects so much of reality, especially when it comes to human emotions, relationships, and the injustices of the world. Beneath all the adventure, humour, and fantasy, there are so many real-life themes that make you think and feel deeply.

articles.title: Taylor Swift wedding-dress fever puts bridal brands on high alert
articles.summary:
Taylor Swift’s wedding dress remains under wraps. But wedding chain David’s Bridal ​is already betting brides will want one just like it.

Fans are eagerly awaiting the reveal of the Christian Dior dress Swift wore at her ‌tightly controlled Madison Square Garden celebration on July 3. Meanwhile, the Hong Kong design team at David’s Bridal, which owns roughly 200 stores across the US, has already sketched about two dozen looks based on the pop star’s likely aesthetics, with a focus on Hollywood glamour and drop-waist silhouettes, CEO Kelly Cook told Reuters.

Those preparations will help the brand “move very quickly when we have an idea of where ​the dress has landed,” Cook explained. David’s Bridal has already seen an uptick in searches for Swift-inspired designs on its website, which lists dresses ranging ​from hundreds of dollars to more than $3,000.

Designers say they will be looking out for elements of her outfit that could blossom into bridal fashion trends.

Viola Chan, head of couture and design at David’s Bridal in Hong Kong, said her team studied Swift’s personal life to sketch three groups of designs: ​embellished ball gowns, simple gowns with a touch of detail, and short dresses in case of a mid-ceremony outfit change.

“It could be her makeup, her hair styling, and could ​be the number of gowns that she changed, the color of her gowns, the floral decoration,” Chan said, while showcasing a template adorned with flowers and lace.

Barcelona-based bridal wear designer Pronovias, with distribution in more than 100 countries, said it plans to draw inspiration from the silhouettes, fabrics and “attitude” of Swift’s look, as the brand has done for royal and other high-profile celebrity weddings in ​the past.

New Swift-Inspired Designs

An unusual color or fabric - pink or metallic lace, for example - could ripple through the bridal industry, said Sharon Sever, the creative director at Tel ​Aviv-based luxury wedding dress company Galia Lahav. A unique veil might also inspire new fashion trends.

For now, brands like Galia Lahav and New York-based Jenny Yoo are in a wait-and-see mode, along ‌with their customers.

“The images make all the difference in the design world,” said Liza Pontoni, design director at Jenny Yoo.

The Justin Alexander Group, a US-based bridal fashion house, is in the process of finalising sketches for its spring and summer 2028 collection, which will be available in stores in autumn 2027. If Swift reveals her Dior dress in the coming weeks, the company might incorporate certain elements into the designs, said CEO and creative director Justin Warshaw.

And if boutiques signal a surge in interest for Swift-inspired gowns, the fashion ​house might pull strings to make the ​new collection available to retailers and brides ⁠even sooner than the typical one-year timeline, Warshaw said.

For indie bridal franchise Lovely Bride, new details will be at most referential to Swift’s look, said Lanie List, the founder and CEO.

“We’ll definitely tell our brides things that we have that are similar, if ​something she wears inspires them,” she said.

Legal Risks

For designers and brands, the risk of falling into legal trouble depends on ​what exactly they copy, said Brad D. Rose, co-chair of law firm Pryor Cashman’s Intellectual Property Group, who works with luxury brands.

US copyright law generally does not protect the cut, shape or silhouette of clothing. That means a bridal company can often lawfully create a dress that mimics an aesthetic. But specific decorative elements such as embroidery or beadwork may be protected.

If a bridal brand were to ​falsely suggest an affiliation with Swift or LVMH-owned Dior, trademark and unfair competition concerns could arise, Rose ​added.

Pronovias leans into seasonal trends rather than emulating specific pieces or names, a spokesperson said.

The designer will, for example, avoid using Swift or Dior’s name in marketing, while still drawing inspiration from trends that emerge ​from the collaboration.

articles.title: Two Nepalis killed on Romanian railway track
articles.summary:
Two Nepalis were killed after being hit by a train in Romania’s eastern city of Bacău early Sunday morning. Their identities have not yet been disclosed.

According to a statement from the Bacău Inspectorate for Emergency Situations (ISU), the two were struck by a train at around 3:21 am while walking along the railway line near Chimiei Street.

Emergency responders, including ambulances, rescue teams and medical personnel, reached the site shortly after receiving information about the incident. They found both individuals dead upon arrival, the ISU said.

Romanian police and railway authorities have launched an investigation into the accident.

“An investigation is underway to establish how they ended up on the railway line and the circumstances that led to the accident,” the ISU said in its statement.

articles.title: Australia tightens student visa rules, rejects 64 percent of Nepali applications
articles.summary:
Australia has rejected around 64 percent of offshore student visa applications from Nepal, marking the highest rejection rate recorded for Nepali applicants, according to official data.

The surge in visa refusals comes after the Australian government tightened its screening process for international students amid concerns over migration levels, housing pressures and the integrity of the education system.

Australia categorises countries under an “Evidence Level” risk framework to determine the level of scrutiny applied during visa processing. Education sector insiders say Nepal was recently moved to “Level 3”, the highest-risk category, from “Level 2” following a government review conducted several months ago.

The impact has been most severe in the vocational education and training (VET) sector, which traditionally attracts students seeking shorter and more affordable courses. Nearly 90 percent of Nepali applications for VET courses have been rejected, with only 56 of 549 applicants receiving visas, according to recent statistics.

Around 60,000 Nepali students are currently enrolled in Australian institutions. Of them, about 56,000 are existing students, while roughly 4,000 are new arrivals.

Data from Australia’s Department of Home Affairs shows a sharp decline in new student arrivals from Nepal. Between January and May this year, only 2,700 of 7,500 offshore applicants from Nepal were granted visas. During the same period last year, 7,167 of 8,028 applicants received approvals.

The uncertainty surrounding visa approvals, combined with rising application costs, has discouraged many prospective students. Applicants currently have to pay an application fee of A$2,500 (approximately Rs260,000), which is non-refundable even if the visa is rejected.

Sanjeev Pandey, a Sydney-based lawyer, said Australia had welcomed a large number of international students after the Covid-19 pandemic, but authorities later became concerned about patterns of students changing courses and extending their stay without completing their original programmes.

“The government may have also tightened student visa rules to address growing employment and housing pressures,” Pandey said.

The stricter visa regime has raised concerns among education consultancies and smaller institutions that rely heavily on international enrolments.

Khagendra Satyal, international business development manager at Central Australian College, said the decline in student arrivals had significantly affected the sector.

“Visas are now granted only after assessing what positive contributions an international student can make to Australia in the long run,” Satyal said. “Students applying from Nepal need to understand this shift.”

The immigration crackdown also comes amid growing political pressure in Australia over migration. Analysts say the rise of politicians with hardline positions on immigration, including Pauline Hanson, has contributed to a broader political push for tighter controls.

Lawyer Pandey said the tougher environment has affected not only prospective students but also those already in Australia. Renewing student visas, switching back to student visas after completing post-study work arrangements, and bringing spouses as dependants have all become more difficult, he said.

Obtaining permanent residency has also become significantly more challenging compared with previous years.

Despite the tightening measures, Nepal remains one of the largest sources of international students in Australia. Government data shows Nepali students account for around nine percent of Australia's international student population, making Nepal the third-largest source country.

articles.title: Budget-friendly places for Nepali students in Ohio
articles.summary:
Athens is a small, scenic college town in southeastern Ohio, shaped largely by Ohio University and its energetic student community. Surrounded by rolling hills, rivers and forests, the town combines historic streets, local businesses and easy access to nature.

The university campus, downtown shops and restaurants are concentrated within a compact area, making daily life manageable without a car. Ohio University students can also use Athens Public Transit free of charge, while nearby trails and forests provide inexpensive options for hiking and outdoor recreation.

Because Athens is a relatively small town, the number of professional internships available locally can be limited. Although Ohio University hosts career fairs and attracts employers from across the country, students may need to look beyond Athens or relocate temporarily for specialised opportunities.

Oxford is a compact, classic college town in southwestern Ohio, built almost entirely around Miami University at its core. Red-brick Georgian buildings, leafy streets and a walkable uptown give it a traditional campus-town character.

The compact layout means campus, uptown restaurants, shops and student housing are all within easy walking distance. The town is also considered quite safe, and Miami University's strong sense of community brings a steady calendar of campus events, traditions and activities that keep student life active without needing to travel elsewhere.

The town's economy is heavily tied to the university, so it can feel quiet or emptied out during breaks and summer months when students are away.

ColumbusColumbus is Ohio's capital and largest city, and it's where The Ohio State University, one of the biggest campuses in the country, is situated. Rather than a self-contained college town, Columbus functions as a full city with sprawling neighborhoods, a job market, and student population that's just one part of a much bigger urban picture.

Pros:Living costs stay reasonable even with everything a major city offers, and students get real exposure to internships and employers across finance, tech, healthcare and government without having to leave town.

Cons:The scale of the city brings more traffic and scattered housing options, so building a close community takes a bit more intention than it would in a smaller town.

Cincinnati is moving to universities like the University of Cincinnati and Xavier University. The city has 300,000 people and many residential areas.

Pros:The city offers people a diverse job market. It is home to many consumer goods, finance and healthcare companies. The cost of living is on the lower end for cities of this size.

Cons:Despite its universities, the city is not generally considered a college town. Younger residents have to actively seek college-town experiences since it is not part of city life. The city is also not walkable.

Toledo is Ohio’s fourth largest city, sitting on the edge of Lake Erie. It is a city of 600,000 people and home to the University of Toledo.

Pros: The University of Toledo sits at the centre of city life. It is the biggest school in town and also the town's biggest employer. Students have a solid pipeline to work experience and internships.

Cons: As a Rust Belt city, its growth has been stagnant over the years. And despite its size, it is considered to be falling behind the other major metros in Ohio.

Based on conversations with local Nepali students in Ohio.

articles.title: Migrant workers can strike under new Qatari labour law
articles.summary:
The Qatari government has introduced a conditional right for migrant workers to stage legal strikes as part of amendments to the country’s labour law.

Under the revised law, workers can go on strike for up to six working days after notifying their employer and the Ministry of Labour in writing, but only if a labour dispute cannot be resolved through negotiation, conciliation or mediation. The provision was introduced through Qatar’s Law No 9 of 2026, which amended the 2004 Labour Law (Law No 14) to strengthen workers’ rights and welfare.

The amended law requires companies with 100 or more employees to establish joint committees made up of management and worker representatives. The committees are intended to improve workplace dialogue, strengthen consultation and help resolve disputes before they escalate.

The reforms also introduce tougher penalties for labour violations. Employers that breach wage protection regulations may face suspension of ministry services, while the Labour Dispute Resolution Committee has been formally authorised to conduct virtual hearings. Recruitment agencies and companies involved in hiring violations may face fines ranging from QAR3,000 to QAR25,000. One Qatari riyal is equivalent to Rs41.66.

Workers exercising their right to strike will not be entitled to wages during the strike period. The law also allows companies to dismiss without notice workers who organise illegal or unjustified strikes without following the required procedures or who disrupt business operations through such actions.

Companies that fail to establish mandatory joint committees may face fines ranging from QAR2,000 to QAR5,000.

Qatar has also strengthened enforcement of its Wage Protection System. The amended law gives the labour ministry greater authority to take action against employers that delay or fail to pay salaries, including suspending services, imposing administrative measures and applying regulatory penalties against repeat offenders.

If a company repeatedly violates wage rules or triggers collective disputes because of unpaid salaries, other companies under the same ownership may also face penalties. The ministry may publish the names of non-compliant companies on its website.

Workers who remain unpaid can request a change of employer or terminate their contracts, with repatriation costs to be covered by the employer.

The Labour Dispute Resolution Committee’s new authority to conduct virtual hearings means workers no longer need to be physically present to pursue labour cases. Employers, workers and verified witnesses can now participate in proceedings online.

Workers must first register disputes with the ministry. Cases are referred to the dispute resolution committee only when efforts to settle them through negotiation fail. Agreements reached through ministry-led mediation will have the status of legally enforceable documents.

The amended law also increases penalties for recruitment-related violations.

Recruitment agencies can be fined between QAR3,000 and QAR25,000 for hiring workers without ministry approval for employment contracts, processing recruitment before mandatory medical examinations or committing other administrative and recruitment-related violations.

Qatari recruitment agencies generally recruit workers in partnership with manpower agencies in Nepal, although some employers also hire directly through Nepali firms.

The new rules also require workers seeking employment in designated technical and professional occupations to obtain certificates confirming that they have completed required training and passed examinations at ministry-approved centres before starting work.

Meanwhile, Qatar has extended the non-compete period, during which an employee can be restricted from joining a competing company after leaving a job, from one year to two years. The change restores a provision that existed before 2020.

If an employee has access to sensitive client information, trade secrets or confidential company data, an employer can prevent them from joining a competitor for up to two years after the termination of employment.

The labour law amendments are aimed at modernising Qatar’s labour market, improving regulatory oversight and creating a more flexible and competitive employment system in line with the Qatar National Vision 2030. Some provisions will require additional decrees and executive regulations before they come into full effect.

“These reforms represent significant shifts that will heavily impact employers, workers, recruitment agencies and the dispute resolution system alike,” Krishna Panthi, president of the Non-Resident Nepali Association Qatar, told Kantipur.

articles.title: भीमफेदीमा कोदोखेती गर्ने किसानलाई अनुदान
articles.summary:
मकवानपुरको भीमफेदी गाउँपालिकाले कोदोबालीतर्फ किसानलाई आकर्षित गर्न नगद अनुदान कार्यक्रम सञ्चालन गर्ने भएको छ।

गाउँपालिकाले आर्थिक वर्ष २०८३ / ०८४ को स्वीकृत वार्षिक कार्यक्रमअनुसार ‘रैथाने बाली खेती प्रोत्साहनका लागि नगद अनुदान कार्यक्रम’ सञ्चालन गर्न लागेको गाउँपालिकाका अध्यक्ष हिदम लामाले जानकारी दिए। 'लोप हुने जोखिममा रहेका रैथाने बाली जोगाउने र कृषिकलाई यसतर्फ आकर्षित गराउने उद्देश्यका साथ हामीले कृषक प्रोत्साहनको यस खालको कार्यक्रम अघि सारेका हौँ', उनले भने, 'पालिकाका सबै वडामा कोदोखेती गर्ने किसान तथा कृषि फर्मले प्रोत्साहन अनुदानका लागि आवेदन दिन सक्नेछन्।'

अध्यक्ष लामाका अनुसार कोदोखेती गरिएको क्षेत्रफल कम्तीमा दुई रोपनी वा सोभन्दा बढी हुनुपर्नेछ। उनका अनुसार यसमा अनुदानको एकाइ भने प्रतिरोपनी निर्धारण गरिएको छ। अनुदानका लागि पालिकाको कृषि विकास शाखाले सूचना प्रकाशित गर्दै भीमफेदी गाउँपालिकामा स्थायी ठेगाना भएका इच्छुक कृषक तथा कृषि फर्मलाई आवेदन आह्वान गरिएको प्रमुख प्रशासकीय अधिकृत चेतनाथ न्यौपानेले जानकारी दिए।'

अनुदानका लागि पालिकाका कृषक तथा कृषि फर्महरुले पालिका कार्यालयको कृषि विकास शाखा वा सम्बन्धित वडा कार्यालयमा आवेदन दर्ता गर्न सक्नेछन्।', प्रमुख प्रशासकीय अधिकृत न्यौपानेले भने। गाउँपालिकाले किसानलाई आर्थिक वर्ष २०८३-०८४ को कृषि कार्यक्रम सञ्चालनसम्बन्धी निर्देशिका-२०८०, संशोधित व्यवस्थाबमोजिम अनुदान उपलब्ध गराइने प्रमुख प्रशासकीय अधिकृत न्यौपानेको भनाई छ।

गाउँपालिकाको स्थानीयस्तरमा परम्परागत रूपमा उत्पादन हुँदै आएको कोदोखेतीलाई पुनः प्रोत्साहन गर्ने नीति लिएकोमा आफूहरुजस्ता कृषकलाई यसमा टिक्न सहजता हुने स्थानीय कृषक विजय पुडासैनीले बताए। 'अहिले विशेषगरी कृषिमा नयाँ तथा बजारमुखी बालीतर्फ किसान आकर्षित भइरहेको बेला गाउँपालिकाले हामीलाई परम्परागत रैथाने बालीको संरक्षणमा सहयोग गर्नु निक्कै नै खुसीको कुरा हो', उनले भने, 'रैथाने बाली लगाउने चलन विस्तारै कमी हुँदै गइरहेको अवस्थामा पालिकाले कोदो खेतीमा गरेको अनुदानको व्यवस्थाले आगामी दिनमा यसको खेती गर्ने पक्कै बढ्नेछन्।'

अनुदान लिन चाहने पालिकाका कृषक तथा फर्मलाई आवेदनसँगै निवेदकको नागरिकताको प्रमाणपत्रको प्रतिलिपि र सम्बन्धित वडा कार्यालयको सिफारिस, फर्म दर्ता प्रमाणपत्र, नवीकरणको प्रमाण, कर चुक्ता प्रमाणपत्र र स्थायी लेखा नम्बर प्रमाणपत्रको प्रतिलिपि उपलब्ध गराउन पालिकाले सूचनासमेत प्रकाशन गर्दै आग्रह गरेको छ। रासस

articles.title: पाँच बोरा प्रतिबन्धित रातो जडिबुटी च्याउसहित महिला नियन्त्रणमा
articles.summary:
जिल्ला प्रहरी कार्यालय सुर्खेतले प्रतिबन्धित जडिबुटी ‘रातो जडिबुटी च्याउ’ सहित एक जनालाई नियन्त्रणमा लिएको छ।

जिल्ला प्रहरी कार्यालय वीरेन्द्रनगरका अनुसार नेपालगञ्जतर्फ जाँदै गरेको बसलाई चेकजाँच गर्ने क्रममा बसको डिक्कीमा लुकाइछिपाइ राखिएको अवस्थामा पाँच बोरा प्रतिबन्धित जडिबुटी फेला परेको हो।

प्रहरीले बरामद गरिएको जडिबुटीको नापतौल गर्दा करिब ४ किलो ७४० ग्राम रहेको जनाएको छ। घटनामा संलग्न रहेको आरोपमा जुम्लाको सिँजा गाउँपालिका–६ घर भई हाल सुर्खेतको वीरेन्द्रनगरमा बस्दै आएकी ३२ वर्षीया चन्द्रकला बुढालाई नियन्त्रणमा लिइएको प्रहरीले जनाएको छ।

प्रहरीका अनुसार चेकजाँचका क्रममा बरामद भएको जडिबुटी र बसलाई समेत नियन्त्रणमा लिई घटनाबारे थप अनुसन्धान भइरहेको छ। प्रतिबन्धित जडिबुटीको ओसारपसार तथा कारोबारमा संलग्न अन्य व्यक्तिको समेत खोजी भइरहेको प्रहरीले जनाएको छ।

प्रहरीले अवैध तथा प्रतिबन्धित जडिबुटीको संकलन, ओसारपसार र कारोबार नियन्त्रणका लागि निगरानी तथा चेकजाँचलाई थप कडाइ गर्ने जनाएको छ।

articles.title: ‘युवा पुस्ताले चाहेको परिवर्तन प्रविधि, उद्यमशीलता र अवसर हो’
articles.summary:
चितवनका युवाले उद्यमशीलतालाई राजनीतिसंग जोड्नुपर्नेमा जोड दिएका छन्। अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय युवा दिवसको अवसरमा राष्ट्रिय स्वतन्त्र पार्टी (रास्वपा) चितवनद्वारा आयोजित कार्यक्रममा ‘मेरो पुस्ताको राजनीति कस्तो हुनुपर्छ?’ विषयमा युवाबीच वक्तृत्वकला, ‘कृषि उद्यमशीलता र युवा समृद्ध नेपालको आधार’ विषयमा विचार-विमर्श तथा सांसदसँग युवा संवाद कार्यक्रका सहभागीको सो उद्यमशीलता विनाको राजनीतिले समृद्धि नआउने सुझाव थियो।

वक्तृत्वकलामा सहभागिता १० युवाले अब भाषणमा सीमित राजनीति नभई परिणाममुखी, प्रविधिमैत्री र उद्यमशील राजनीतिक संस्कार खोजेको धारणा व्यक्त गरे।

राजनीति जनताको सेवा गर्ने माध्यम बन्नुपर्ने जनाउँदै उनीहरूले राजनीतिमा युवा सहभागिता मात्रै नभई नीति निर्माण र कार्यान्वयनमा समेत युवाको अर्थपूर्ण भूमिका सुनिश्चित गर्नुपर्ने बताए।

प्रविधिमैत्री सेवा, चुस्त प्रशासन, पारदर्शिता र जवाफदेहितालाई अहिलेको आवश्यकता भएको भन्दै राजनीति फोहोरी खेल नभई जनताको माया र विश्वास प्राप्त गर्ने माध्यम बन्नुपर्ने उनीहरूको भनाइ थियो। ‘जेनजी’ पुस्ताले चाहेको परिवर्तन पनि प्रविधि, उद्यमशीलता र अवसरसँग जोडिएको उनीहरूले बताए।

राजनीतिमा सहभागिता मात्रै खोजेर नपुग्ने भन्दै नीति तथा नियम निर्माणमा समेत आफ्नो भूमिका स्थापित गर्नुपर्ने, राजनीतिमा पारदर्शिता, जवाफदेहिता, समावेशिता र सशक्तीकरणलाई प्राथमिकता दिनुपर्ने, प्रविधिको पहुँच सबै नागरिकसम्म पुर्‍याउनुपर्ने, आगामी पुस्तालाई सहयोग पुग्ने नीति बनाउनुपर्ने तथा सरकारलाई पूर्ण रूपमा डिजिटल र पारदर्शी बनाउनुपर्ने, शिक्षा जीवनका समस्या समाधान गर्न सक्ने खालको हुनुपर्ने, अनुसन्धानमा लगानी बढाउनुपर्ने तथा स्वास्थ्य क्षेत्रलाई प्राथमिकता दिनुपर्ने युवाहरूको माग थियो।

रोजगारीका लागि विदेशिनुपर्ने अवस्थाको अन्त्य गर्दै ‘रेमिट्यान्स’मा मात्रै निर्भर नभई स्वदेशमै उद्यमशीलता र रोजगारीका अवसर सिर्जना गर्नुपर्ने सहभागी युवाहरुले धारणा राखेका थिए। दश जना युवा सहभागिता रहेको वक्तृत्वकला प्रतियोगितामा अमृत ढकाल प्रथम, निरिता पौडेल द्धितीय र आयुस्मा श्रेष्ठ तृतीय भएका थिए।

पत्रकार विवेक पोखरेलले कृषिविज्ञ डा भानेश्वर पोखरेल, भवानी डेरीका सञ्चालक सुवास पौडेल तथा चितवनमा सयपत्रीलगायत फूलको बगैँचाबाट सफल व्यवसाय सञ्चालन गर्दै आएकी सुजाता देवकोटासँग कृषि उद्यमशीलताका विषयमा विचार–विमर्श गरेका थिए।

उनीहरूले कृषिलाई सम्मानित व्यवसायका रूपमा विकास गर्न, आधुनिक प्रविधि, अनुसन्धान र बजार व्यवस्थापनमा लगानी बढाउन तथा युवा र शिक्षित जनशक्तिलाई कृषि उद्यमशीलतामा जोडेर आत्मनिर्भर बनाउनुपर्नेमा जोड दिए।

चितवन क्षेत्र नं १ का सांसद तथा राज्य व्यवस्था तथा सुशासन समिति सभापति हरि ढकालले युवाले काम गर्दै जाँदा भएका त्रुटि सच्याउँदै अघि बढ्नुपर्ने बताए। उनले गल्ती गर्न हुँदैन भन्नेभन्दा पनि गल्तीबाट सिकेर आफ्नो लगनशीलताका साथ अघि बढ्नुपर्नेमा जोड दिए।

काम गर्नेहरूलाई सिर्जनात्मक खबरदारी आवश्यक रहेको जनाउँदै उनले खबरदारी, कार्यसम्पादन र भाषण फरक विषय भएको उल्लेख गरे। राजनीतिक नेतृत्वले भाषणभन्दा काम र नतिजामा ध्यान दिनुपर्ने उनको भनाइ थियो।

सांसद प्रभा ढकालले स्थानीय तहलाई जवाफदेही बनाउन आवश्यक छ भने। सांसदहरू नीति तथा नियम निर्माणका काममा केन्द्रित हुने गरेको र आवश्यकता अनुसार सम्बन्धित विषयमा भूमिका निर्वाह गर्दै आएको उनको भनाइ थियो।

रास्वपा चितवनका जिल्ला सभापति इन्जिनियर मिनिमाधव खनालको सभापतित्वमा सम्पन्न कार्यक्रममा रास्वपा केन्द्रीय सदस्य सविना विक, आकाक्षा पोखरेल र पवित्रा थापा, जिल्ला सचिव तेजेन्द्रप्रसाद पौडेल, उपसभापति निर्मला गिरी, जिल्ला सहसचिव कुशल पाठक, केन्द्रीय महाधिवेशन प्रतिनिधि, प्रदेश सदस्य, क्षेत्रीय सभापति, जिल्ला कार्यसमिति तथा पालिका र वडा प्रतिनिधि लगायतको सहभागिता थियो।

articles.title: रोल्पा पहिरो : दुई जनाको मृत्यु, १० बेपत्ता
articles.summary:
रोल्पामा बुधबार साँझ परेको भीषण वर्षापछि आएको पहिरोले घर पुरिँदा २ जनाको मृत्यु भएको छ भने २ जना घाइते भएका छन्। पहिरोमा परी १० जना बेपत्ता छन्।

रोल्पा प्रहरीका अनुसार रोल्पाको थबाङ गाउँपालिका–५ बोटलबारामा रातिकरिब ९ बजेतिर घरमाथिबाट पहिरो झरेको थियो।

स्थानीयका अनुसार त्यहाँ करिब आधा दर्जन घरगोठ पुरिएका छन्। पहिरोमा परी मृत्यु हुनेमा थबाङ गाउँपालिका–५ बोटलबाराका वर्ष ६० का कमलबहादुर पुन मगर र वर्ष १८ की शान्ती पुन मगर रहेका छन्। भने २२ वर्षीय हिमाल पुन मगर र २५ वर्षीय संजय घर्तीमगर घाइते भएका छन्।

घाइतेलाई प्रहरी र स्थानीयको सहयोगमा उद्धार गरी प्राथमिक उपचार भइरहेको र थप उपचारका लागि जिल्ला बाहिर पठाउने तयारी भइरहेको जनाइएको छ। प्रहरीका अनुसार घाइतेको अवस्था गम्भीर छ। अन्य व्यक्ति पनि पहिरोले पुरिएको हुन सक्ने भन्दै स्थानिय र प्रहरीले थप खोजिकार्य गर्दैछ।

सदरमुकामबाट २८ कोष टाटाको यो ठाउँमा थप उद्धारका लागि सदमुकामबाट प्रमुख जिल्ला अधिकारी गंगाबहादुर क्षेत्री, प्रहरी प्रमुख डिएसपी पंचकुमार बाखु, नेपाली सेनाका कर्णेलदिपेश खड्का, सशस्त्र डिएसपी कालिप्रशाद चौधरीसहितको टोलीलगायत घटनास्थल लागेका छन्।

घटनास्थल नजिकै पुगेका प्रमुख जिल्ला अधिकारी प्रमुख जिल्ला अधिकारीले सदरमुकामबाट हिडेको सेना, प्रहरी र सशस्त्र प्रहरीको थप उद्धार टोली पनि केहीबेरमा घटनास्थल पुग्ने बताए। ‘ठुलो पहिरो आएको छ। २ जनाको मृत्यु, २ जना घाइते र १० जना बेपत्ता रहेको अहिले सम्मको अवस्था हो। घाइतेलाई स्थानीय र प्रहरीको सहयोगमा स्वास्थ्यकर्मीसहित प्राथमिक स्वास्थ्य केन्द्र सुलिचौर पठाइएको छ।’

articles.title: भीमफेदीमा कोदोखेती गर्ने किसानलाई अनुदान
articles.summary:
मकवानपुरको भीमफेदी गाउँपालिकाले कोदोबालीतर्फ किसानलाई आकर्षित गर्न नगद अनुदान कार्यक्रम सञ्चालन गर्ने भएको छ।

गाउँपालिकाले आर्थिक वर्ष २०८३ / ०८४ को स्वीकृत वार्षिक कार्यक्रमअनुसार ‘रैथाने बाली खेती प्रोत्साहनका लागि नगद अनुदान कार्यक्रम’ सञ्चालन गर्न लागेको गाउँपालिकाका अध्यक्ष हिदम लामाले जानकारी दिए। 'लोप हुने जोखिममा रहेका रैथाने बाली जोगाउने र कृषिकलाई यसतर्फ आकर्षित गराउने उद्देश्यका साथ हामीले कृषक प्रोत्साहनको यस खालको कार्यक्रम अघि सारेका हौँ', उनले भने, 'पालिकाका सबै वडामा कोदोखेती गर्ने किसान तथा कृषि फर्मले प्रोत्साहन अनुदानका लागि आवेदन दिन सक्नेछन्।'

अध्यक्ष लामाका अनुसार कोदोखेती गरिएको क्षेत्रफल कम्तीमा दुई रोपनी वा सोभन्दा बढी हुनुपर्नेछ। उनका अनुसार यसमा अनुदानको एकाइ भने प्रतिरोपनी निर्धारण गरिएको छ। अनुदानका लागि पालिकाको कृषि विकास शाखाले सूचना प्रकाशित गर्दै भीमफेदी गाउँपालिकामा स्थायी ठेगाना भएका इच्छुक कृषक तथा कृषि फर्मलाई आवेदन आह्वान गरिएको प्रमुख प्रशासकीय अधिकृत चेतनाथ न्यौपानेले जानकारी दिए।'

अनुदानका लागि पालिकाका कृषक तथा कृषि फर्महरुले पालिका कार्यालयको कृषि विकास शाखा वा सम्बन्धित वडा कार्यालयमा आवेदन दर्ता गर्न सक्नेछन्।', प्रमुख प्रशासकीय अधिकृत न्यौपानेले भने। गाउँपालिकाले किसानलाई आर्थिक वर्ष २०८३-०८४ को कृषि कार्यक्रम सञ्चालनसम्बन्धी निर्देशिका-२०८०, संशोधित व्यवस्थाबमोजिम अनुदान उपलब्ध गराइने प्रमुख प्रशासकीय अधिकृत न्यौपानेको भनाई छ।

गाउँपालिकाको स्थानीयस्तरमा परम्परागत रूपमा उत्पादन हुँदै आएको कोदोखेतीलाई पुनः प्रोत्साहन गर्ने नीति लिएकोमा आफूहरुजस्ता कृषकलाई यसमा टिक्न सहजता हुने स्थानीय कृषक विजय पुडासैनीले बताए। 'अहिले विशेषगरी कृषिमा नयाँ तथा बजारमुखी बालीतर्फ किसान आकर्षित भइरहेको बेला गाउँपालिकाले हामीलाई परम्परागत रैथाने बालीको संरक्षणमा सहयोग गर्नु निक्कै नै खुसीको कुरा हो', उनले भने, 'रैथाने बाली लगाउने चलन विस्तारै कमी हुँदै गइरहेको अवस्थामा पालिकाले कोदो खेतीमा गरेको अनुदानको व्यवस्थाले आगामी दिनमा यसको खेती गर्ने पक्कै बढ्नेछन्।'

अनुदान लिन चाहने पालिकाका कृषक तथा फर्मलाई आवेदनसँगै निवेदकको नागरिकताको प्रमाणपत्रको प्रतिलिपि र सम्बन्धित वडा कार्यालयको सिफारिस, फर्म दर्ता प्रमाणपत्र, नवीकरणको प्रमाण, कर चुक्ता प्रमाणपत्र र स्थायी लेखा नम्बर प्रमाणपत्रको प्रतिलिपि उपलब्ध गराउन पालिकाले सूचनासमेत प्रकाशन गर्दै आग्रह गरेको छ। रासस

articles.title: Two killed, 10 missing after landslide buries homes in Rolpa
articles.summary:
The death toll from a landslide in Rolpa has risen to three, with nine people still missing after heavy rain sent a torrent of mud and debris down a hillside in Thabang Rural Municipality-5 on Wednesday night.

The landslide struck Kotlabara at around 8:40 pm, burying houses, shops and cattle sheds where about seven families lived. Two people were seriously injured and rescued from the debris.

The latest death was that of 71-year-old Manarkhi Pun Magar, whose body was recovered from the debris on Thursday. The other victims were 18-year-old Shanti Pun Magar and 60-year-old Kamal Bahadur Pun Magar, according to the Lumbini Province Police Office.

The nine people still missing have been identified as 40-year-old Jun Kumari Pun Magar, nine-year-old Ashim Pun Magar, six-year-old Ashok Pun Magar, 75-year-old Dal Bahadur Pun Magar, 80-year-old Ajambar Pun Magar, 78-year-old Bal Bahadur Pun Magar, 72-year-old Lil Bahadur Pun Magar, 71-year-old Mani Pun Magar and 67-year-old Hastakala Roka Magar.

The injured, 22-year-old Himal Pun Magar and 25-year-old Sanjay Gharti Magar, were pulled from the debris by police and local residents and taken towards Sulaichaur for treatment.

The Area Police Office in Uwa was alerted at around 9:30 pm. A police team reached the site at about 10:15 pm and continued the search through the night. Rescue efforts resumed early Thursday as security personnel and residents worked to clear debris and locate those still missing.

Local health worker Bimarsh Gharti Magar said the steep and difficult terrain was hampering rescue efforts and making it difficult to reach the injured and those believed to be trapped.

Deputy Superintendent of Police Pancha Kumar Bakhu, Rolpa police chief, said the search and rescue operation was continuing and that more details would become available as rescuers made progress.

The landslide struck an area about 80 kilometres northeast of Liwang, the district headquarters. The Uwa area is considered highly vulnerable to landslides. A landslide in a nearby village several years ago killed at least six people.

The story has been updated.

articles.title: अर्ना र चराचुरुङ्गीले परिचित कोशी टप्पु, पर्यटककाे रोजाइमा
articles.summary:
दुर्लभ वन्यजन्तु, सयौँ प्रजातिका चराचुरुङ्गी र प्रकृतिमा आधारित पर्यटनको सम्भावनाका कारण कोशी टप्पु आरक्ष क्षेत्र पछिल्ला वर्षमा आन्तरिक तथा विदेशी पर्यटकको आकर्षक गन्तव्य बन्दै गएको छ।

अन्तरराष्ट्रिय महत्व बोकेको यस सिमसार क्षेत्रमा दैनिक रूपमा स्वदेशी तथा विदेशी पर्यटक कोशी टप्पु पुग्ने गरेका छन्। यो वन्यजन्तु आरक्ष सुनसरी, सप्तरी र उदयपुरको बीचमा फैलिएको संरक्षित क्षेत्र हो।

विसं २०३२ मा स्थापना भएको आरक्ष प्रारम्भमा १७५ वर्ग किलोमिटर क्षेत्रफलमा फैलिएको थियो। २०६१ मा मध्यवर्ती क्षेत्र थपिएपछि यसको क्षेत्रफल १७३ वर्ग किलोमिटर कायम भएको छ। सप्तकोशी नदीले बनाएको टापुमा अवस्थित यो आरक्ष नेपालमा प्राकृतिक रूपमा पाइने जङ्गली भैँसी (अर्ना) को मुख्य बासस्थानका रूपमा परिचित छ।

आरक्षभित्र सप्तकोशीले बनाएका बालुवाको टापु, सिसौँ र खयरका वन, बसाइँसराइ गर्ने चराचुरुङ्गी तथा अति दुर्लभ खरमयूरका वासस्थान रहेका छन्। सन् १९८७ देखि रामसार सूचीमा सूचीकृत यस क्षेत्रमा घडियाल, मगरगोही, डल्फिन र विभिन्न प्रजातिका माछा पाइन्छन्। चराहरूको अत्यधिक विविधताका कारण कोशी टप्पुलाई चराहरूको राजधानी पनि भनिन्छ।

नेपालको पर्यटन उद्योग नयाँ गन्तव्यको खोजीमा रहेका बेला वन्यजन्तु अवलोकन, पन्छी अवलोकन, फोटोग्राफी पर्यटन र इको टुरिजमका लागि कोशी टप्पु उत्कृष्ट गन्तव्यका रूपमा उभिएको छ। कोशी टप्पु वन्यजन्तु आरक्षका रेन्जर अङ्कित पौडेलका अनुसार, हिमाल, पहाड र तराईको विशिष्ट जैविक विविधता, लोपोन्मुख वन्यजन्तु, जलचर र पन्छीका कारण नेपाल प्रकृति प्रेमी, अनुसन्धानकर्ता र पर्यटकका लागि विश्वकै आकर्षक गन्तव्य बन्दै गएको छ।

पछिल्ला वर्षमा आरक्षमा आन्तरिक पर्यटकको आकर्षण बढ्दै गएको छ। आरक्ष कार्यालयका अनुसार आर्थिक वर्ष २०८१-८२ मा कूल ११ हजार ६०३ पर्यटकले आरक्ष भ्रमण गरेका थिए। तीमध्ये पाँच हजार ९२४ महिला र पाँच हजार ६७९ पुरुष थिए। भ्रमणकर्तामध्ये ११ हजार २१४ जना आन्तरिक पर्यटक, सार्क मुलुकबाट ८७ जना र अन्य मुलुकबाट ३०२ जना विदेशी पर्यटक रहेका थिए।

सो वर्ष सबैभन्दा बढी फागुनमा एक हजार ६९३ पर्यटकले आरक्ष भ्रमण गरेका थिए। त्यसपछि चैतमा एक हजार ६२४, पुसमा एक हजार ४५७, असारमा एक हजार ३५३, वैशाखमा एक हजार २२६, कात्तिकमा एक हजार ७५, माघमा एक हजार ८८, मङ्सिरमा एक हजार ६६, जेठमा ७२२, भदौमा ६८५, असोजमा ४२० र साउनमा १९४ जना पर्यटक पुगेका थिए।

चालु आर्थिक वर्ष २०८२-८३ को जेठ मसान्तसम्म नौ हजार २४२ पर्यटकले आरक्ष भ्रमण गरिसकेका छन्। साउनमा ४९६, भदौमा ५४७, असोजमा ३२५, कात्तिकमा ५९१, मङ्सिरमा एक हजार ८९३, पुसमा ६४२, माघमा एक हजार ४९९, फागुनमा ६९७, चैतमा ६९१, वैशाखमा ७९१ र जेठमा एक हजार ७० पर्यटकले आरक्ष अवलोकन गरेका छन्।

सप्तकोशी नदीको बहावसँगै फैलिएको हरियाली, दुर्लभ अर्नाको बथान, चराचुरुङ्गीको चहलपहल र जलचरको जीवन्त उपस्थितिले कोशी टप्पुलाई जैविक विविधताको अनुपम आश्रयस्थलका रूपमा स्थापित गरेको छ। जैविक विविधताको दृष्टिले नेपालकै महत्वपूर्ण संरक्षित क्षेत्रमध्ये एक मानिने यन संरक्षणसँगै पर्यटन प्रवर्द्धनको ठूलो सम्भावना समेत रहेको छ।

सन् १९७६ को गणनामा कोशी टप्पुमा ६३ वटा अर्ना रहेका थिए भने सन् २०२१ को गणनाअनुसार सङ्ख्या बढेर चार सय ९८ पुगेको कोशी टप्पु बन्यजन्तु आरक्षका रेन्जर पौडेलले बताए। कोशी टप्पुमा ४२ प्रजातिका स्तनधारी, ५३५ प्रजातिका पन्छी, १४१ प्रजातिका माछा र ७७ प्रजातिका पुतली पाइन्छन्। विसं २०८० को गणनाअनुसार ३२ वटा खरमयुर तथा २०७९ को गणनाअनुसार १९ वटा डल्फिन अभिलेख गरिएको छ।

कोशी टप्पुमा विशेषगरी साइबेरिया,चीन, मङ्गोलिया र मध्य एसियाबाट जाडो छल्न आउने प्रवासी चराहरूको ठूलो सङ्ख्या देखिन्छ। चराविज्ञ अनिस तिमल्सिनाका अनुसार कोशी टप्पु उत्तरी गोलाद्र्धबाट आउने चराहरूको प्रमुख विश्रामस्थल हो। यदि चराहरूले विमानस्थल बनाउने हो भने नेपालमा उनीहरूको अन्तरराष्ट्रिय विमानस्थल कोशी टप्पु नै हुन्थ्यो। उनले भने, हिउँदयाम सुरु भएपछि चराहरू यन केही महिना बिताएर गर्मी सुरु हुनासाथ आफ्नै गन्तव्यतर्फ फर्कन्छन्।

कोशी टप्पुको अर्को प्रमुख आकर्षण नेपालमा प्राकृतिक रूपमा पाइने एकमात्र जङ्गली भैँसी (अर्ना) को मुख्य बासस्थान हुनु हो। आरक्षका विशाल घाँसे मैदान अर्नाका लागि उपयुक्त आवास मानिन्छन्। घाँस चरिदिने, बीउ फैलाउने र खुला चरन क्षेत्रको संरक्षणमा अर्नाले महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका खेल्ने संरक्षणकर्मीहरू बताउँछन्।

जङ्गली हात्ती, एकसिङ्गे गैँडा, निलगाई, चितल, रतुवा, लगुना, मलाह बिरालो, घडियाल, मगरगोही, अजिङ्गर, सुनगोहोरोलगायतका दुर्लभ प्रजाति पनि पाइन्छन्। यस जैविक सम्पदाले कोशी टप्पुलाई अनुसन्धान, अध्ययन र प्रकृति पर्यटनका लागि विशिष्ट केन्द्र बनाएको छ।

दुर्लभ अर्ना, प्रवासी चराचुरुङ्गी, जलचर र हरियालीले सजिएको कोशी टप्पु संरक्षण र पर्यटनलाई सँगसँगै अघि बढाउने नेपालको महत्वपूर्ण प्राकृतिक सम्पदाका रूपमा स्थापित हुँदै गएको छ। आरक्षको वनस्पति विविधता पनि उत्तिकै समृद्ध छ। यहाँ सिसौँ, खयर, सेमल, कदम्ब, साज र बाँसलगायत नदी किनारका वन तथा विशाल घाँसे मैदान पाइन्छन्।यिनै घाँसे मैदान अर्ना, हरिण र नीलगाईजस्ता वन्यजन्तुको मुख्य आश्रयस्थल मानिन्छन्।

स्थानीयका अनुसार कोशी टप्पुको जैविक विविधता, नदी प्रणाली, दुर्लभ वन्यजन्तु र स्थानीय संस्कृति नै यसको सबैभन्दा ठूलो सम्पत्ति हो। यी सम्भावनालाई योजनाबद्ध रूपमा पर्यटन उत्पादनमा रूपान्तरण गर्न पूर्वाधार विकास, प्रभावकारी प्रचारप्रसार र संरक्षणलाई सँगसँगै अघि बढाउन आवश्यक रहेको स्थानीयको भनाइ छ।

इटहरीबाट साथीहरूसँग घुम्न आएकी सरिता श्रेष्ठले कोशी टप्पुको प्राकृतिक सौन्दर्य, चराचुरुङ्गी अवलोकन तथा हात्ती र अर्ना हेर्ने अवसर विशेष आकर्षण भएको बताइन्। फुर्सदको समयमा हामी प्रायः यहाँ साथीहरुसँग आउने गर्छौं उनले भनिन्।

स्थानीय होटल व्यवसायी लोकबहादुर मगरका अनुसार कोशी टप्पुको पर्यटन विकास अझै प्रारम्भिक चरणमै छ। सीमित आवास सुविधा, कमजोर सडक पहुँच, अन्य पर्यटकीय पूर्वाधारको अभाव, प्रभावकारी प्रचारप्रसार नहुनु र पर्याप्त लगानीको कमीका कारण आरक्षको वास्तविक पर्यटन सम्भावनाको पूर्ण उपयोग हुन सकेको छैन।

उनका अनुसार कोशी टप्पुमा जङ्गल सफारी, प्रकृति पदयात्रा र स्थानीय संस्कृति अनुभव गर्ने गतिविधिप्रति पर्यटकको रुचि बढ्दै गएको छ। परिवारसँग बसेर ग्रामीण जीवनशैली, परम्परागत खानपान र संस्कृतिको अनुभव गर्न सकिने भएकाले कोशी टप्पु आसपासमा व्यवस्थित होमस्टेहरु विस्तार गर्नसके पर्यटक आगमन अझ बढ्न सक्ने उनको भनाइ छ। रासस

articles.title: देउवाको स्वागतका लागि भेला हुन तोकियो तीन स्थान
articles.summary:
छ महिनामा स्वदेश फर्किन लागेका नेपाली कांग्रेसका पूर्वसभापति शेरबहादुर देउवाको स्वागतका लागि भेला हुन तीनवटा स्थान तोकिएको छ।

कांग्रेसको संस्थापन इतर समूहका नेताहरूले विमानस्थल प्रवेश गर्ने गोल्डेन गेटको अगाडिको खाली ठाउँ, नमस्ते गेटको अगाडिको खाली ठाउँ र तिलगंगा आँखा अस्पताल अगाडिको खाली ठाउँमा कार्यकर्ता भेला हुने ठाउँ तय गरेका हुन्।

उपचारका नाममा विदेश गएको उनी बिहीबार मध्यान्ह साढे १२ बजे काठमाडौं अवतरण हुने छन्।

कांग्रेसको संस्थापन इतर समूहले पूर्वसभापति देउवालाई त्रिभुवन अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय विमानस्थलमा बाजागाजा र सांस्कृतिक झाँकीसहित स्वागतको तयारी गरेको छ।

स्वदेश फर्किएपछि देउवा शुक्रबार सुकेधारास्थित मिराकल पार्टी प्यालेसमा आयोजना हुने इतर समूहको राष्ट्रिय भेलामा सहभागी हुने छन्।

जेनजी आन्दोलनका क्रममा भएको सांघातिक आक्रमणमा परी घाइते भएका पूर्वसभापति देउवा फागुन १३ गते राति सिंगापुर एयरलाइन्सको उडानबाट सिंगापुर गएका थिए। उनी थप उपचारका लागि भन्दै सिंगापुरबाट हङकङ पुगेका थिए।

देउवाको स्वागतका लागि राष्ट्रिय भेला आयोजक समितिका संयोजक डा. शशांक कोइरालाको नेतृत्वमा शीर्ष नेताहरू विमानस्थल पुग्ने छन्।

देउवा त्रिभुवन अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय विमानस्थलमा ओर्लिएपछि नेता–कार्यकर्ताले सांस्कृतिक बाजागाजासहितको झाँकीले स्कर्टिङ गरेर लैजाने तयारी छ।

articles.title: सार्वजनिक लेखा समिति हुर्मत लिने थलो होइन : रामकुमारी झाँक्री
articles.summary:
नेकपा एमालेकी नेतृ एवं राष्ट्रियसभा सदस्य रामकुमारी झाँक्रीले संसदको सार्वजनिक लेखा समिति सरकारी निकाय तथा सार्वजनिक व्यक्तिको ‘हुर्मत लिने थलो’ नभएको बताएकी छन्।

सार्वजनिक लेखा समितिको पछिल्लो बैठकमा भएको छलफलप्रति असन्तुष्टि जनाउँदै झाँक्रीले संविधान र विधिको मर्यादाभित्र रहेर काम गर्न सबै पक्षलाई आग्रह गरिन्।

'संसदको सार्वजनिक लेखा समिति सरकारी निकाय र सार्वजनिक व्यक्तिको हुर्मत लिने थलो होइन। याद रहोस, संविधान र विधिको मर्यादामा हामी सबै बस्नुपर्छ,' उनले भनिन्।

झाँक्रीले सामाजिक सञ्जालमार्फत सार्वजनिक लेखा समितिले आफूले सम्हाल्न नसक्ने र निष्कर्षमा पुर्‍याउन नसक्ने विषयमा केवल सार्वजनिक खपतका लागि हात हाल्न नहुने बताएकी हुन्। उनका अनुसार कुनै व्यक्ति वा संगठनको नेतृत्वमाथि ‘यति खायौ, उति खायौ’ जस्ता आरोपसहित आएका उजुरीलाई पर्याप्त आधार र तयारीबिना समितिको छलफलको एजेण्डा बनाउनु उचित हुँदैन।

‘भ्रष्टाचारको अनुसन्धान गर्ने अर्कै संवैधानिक निकाय छ,’ झाँक्रीले भनेकी छन्, ‘खाएको हो–होइन भन्ने विषयमा तत्काल आन्तरिक लेखापरीक्षण हुन्छ। त्यसको काम महालेखा नियन्त्रकको कार्यालयले गर्छ। फाइनल अडिट गर्ने संवैधानिक निकाय महालेखा परीक्षकको कार्यालय हो।’

महालेखा परीक्षकको प्रतिवेदन हेर्ने निकाय संसद भएको उल्लेख गर्दै उनले सार्वजनिक लेखा समिति संसदको सानो रूप भएकाले विषयलाई निर्धारित प्रक्रियामार्फत अघि बढाउनुपर्नेमा जोड दिएकी छन्। ‘प्रोसेसमा जाने कि यस्तै खपतका काम गर्ने?’ उनले प्रश्न गरेकी छन्।

झाँक्रीले समितिमा हुने छलफलमा संसदीय आचारसंहिता, भाषा र मर्यादालाई समेत ख्याल गर्नुपर्ने बताएकी छन्। सार्वजनिक संस्था र व्यक्तिको अनावश्यक रूपमा हुर्मत लिन नहुने उनको भनाइ छ।

उनले समितिले उजुरीमाथि प्रारम्भिक छनोट (स्क्रिनिङ) गरेर मात्र छलफलका लागि अघि बढाउनुपर्ने सुझाव दिँदै सार्वजनिक लेखा समितिको ध्यानाकर्षण गराएकी छन्।

‘फेरि पनि भन्छु, हिजो जे भयो पटक्कै राम्रो भएन,’ झाँक्रीले भनेकी छन्।

articles.title: मुख्यमन्त्री शाहले आज विश्वासको मत लिँदै
articles.summary:
सुदूरपश्चिम प्रदेशसभाको बैठक आज अपराह्न ५ः०० बजे बस्दैछ।

बैठकमा मुख्यमन्त्री कमलबहादुर शाहले विश्वासको मत लिने कार्यसूची रहेको प्रदेशसभा सचिवालयका सूचना अधिकारी उपसचिव ताराकुमारी जोशीले जानकारी दिइन्।

यस्तै, विगत लामो समयदेखि बैठकमा अनुपस्थित प्रदेशसभा सदस्यका विषयमा पनि छलफल हुने सम्भावित कार्यसूचीमा रहेको उनले बताइन्। सत्ता गठबन्धनमा रहेको नेपाल कम्युनिष्ट पार्टी (एमाले) ले गत असार ३१ गते समर्थन फिर्ता लिएपछि मुख्यमन्त्री शाहले विश्वासको मत लिन लागेका हुन्। संवैधानिक व्यवस्थाअनुसार ३० दिनभित्र विश्वासको मत वा राजीनामा दिनुपर्ने प्रावधानअनुरुप उनले विश्वासको मत दिन लागेका हुन्।

बुधबार सभामुख भीमबहादुर भण्डारीलाई विश्वासको मत लिने जानकारी गराउँदै मुख्यमन्त्री शाहले प्रदेशसभा बैठक आह्वानका लागि पत्र पठाएका थिए। सुदूरपश्चिम प्रदेशसभामा ५३ जना सदस्य रहेका छन्। तीमध्ये मुख्यमन्त्री शाह नेतृत्वको नेपाली कांग्रेसबाट १८, नेपाली कम्युनिष्ट पार्टीबाट सभामुखसहित २२, एमालेबाट ११ र राष्ट्रिय प्रजातन्त्र पार्टीबाट एक जना प्रदेशसभा सदस्य रहेका छन्।

सरकार गठन वा विश्वासको मतका पक्षमा २७ जना आवश्यक पर्छन्। हाल एक जना देश बाहिर र एक जना निलम्बनमा रहेको प्रदेशसभा सचिवालयले जनाएको छ। रासस

articles.title: अर्ना र चराचुरुङ्गीले परिचित कोशी टप्पु, पर्यटककाे रोजाइमा
articles.summary:
दुर्लभ वन्यजन्तु, सयौँ प्रजातिका चराचुरुङ्गी र प्रकृतिमा आधारित पर्यटनको सम्भावनाका कारण कोशी टप्पु आरक्ष क्षेत्र पछिल्ला वर्षमा आन्तरिक तथा विदेशी पर्यटकको आकर्षक गन्तव्य बन्दै गएको छ।

अन्तरराष्ट्रिय महत्व बोकेको यस सिमसार क्षेत्रमा दैनिक रूपमा स्वदेशी तथा विदेशी पर्यटक कोशी टप्पु पुग्ने गरेका छन्। यो वन्यजन्तु आरक्ष सुनसरी, सप्तरी र उदयपुरको बीचमा फैलिएको संरक्षित क्षेत्र हो।

विसं २०३२ मा स्थापना भएको आरक्ष प्रारम्भमा १७५ वर्ग किलोमिटर क्षेत्रफलमा फैलिएको थियो। २०६१ मा मध्यवर्ती क्षेत्र थपिएपछि यसको क्षेत्रफल १७३ वर्ग किलोमिटर कायम भएको छ। सप्तकोशी नदीले बनाएको टापुमा अवस्थित यो आरक्ष नेपालमा प्राकृतिक रूपमा पाइने जङ्गली भैँसी (अर्ना) को मुख्य बासस्थानका रूपमा परिचित छ।

आरक्षभित्र सप्तकोशीले बनाएका बालुवाको टापु, सिसौँ र खयरका वन, बसाइँसराइ गर्ने चराचुरुङ्गी तथा अति दुर्लभ खरमयूरका वासस्थान रहेका छन्। सन् १९८७ देखि रामसार सूचीमा सूचीकृत यस क्षेत्रमा घडियाल, मगरगोही, डल्फिन र विभिन्न प्रजातिका माछा पाइन्छन्। चराहरूको अत्यधिक विविधताका कारण कोशी टप्पुलाई चराहरूको राजधानी पनि भनिन्छ।

नेपालको पर्यटन उद्योग नयाँ गन्तव्यको खोजीमा रहेका बेला वन्यजन्तु अवलोकन, पन्छी अवलोकन, फोटोग्राफी पर्यटन र इको टुरिजमका लागि कोशी टप्पु उत्कृष्ट गन्तव्यका रूपमा उभिएको छ। कोशी टप्पु वन्यजन्तु आरक्षका रेन्जर अङ्कित पौडेलका अनुसार, हिमाल, पहाड र तराईको विशिष्ट जैविक विविधता, लोपोन्मुख वन्यजन्तु, जलचर र पन्छीका कारण नेपाल प्रकृति प्रेमी, अनुसन्धानकर्ता र पर्यटकका लागि विश्वकै आकर्षक गन्तव्य बन्दै गएको छ।

पछिल्ला वर्षमा आरक्षमा आन्तरिक पर्यटकको आकर्षण बढ्दै गएको छ। आरक्ष कार्यालयका अनुसार आर्थिक वर्ष २०८१-८२ मा कूल ११ हजार ६०३ पर्यटकले आरक्ष भ्रमण गरेका थिए। तीमध्ये पाँच हजार ९२४ महिला र पाँच हजार ६७९ पुरुष थिए। भ्रमणकर्तामध्ये ११ हजार २१४ जना आन्तरिक पर्यटक, सार्क मुलुकबाट ८७ जना र अन्य मुलुकबाट ३०२ जना विदेशी पर्यटक रहेका थिए।

सो वर्ष सबैभन्दा बढी फागुनमा एक हजार ६९३ पर्यटकले आरक्ष भ्रमण गरेका थिए। त्यसपछि चैतमा एक हजार ६२४, पुसमा एक हजार ४५७, असारमा एक हजार ३५३, वैशाखमा एक हजार २२६, कात्तिकमा एक हजार ७५, माघमा एक हजार ८८, मङ्सिरमा एक हजार ६६, जेठमा ७२२, भदौमा ६८५, असोजमा ४२० र साउनमा १९४ जना पर्यटक पुगेका थिए।

चालु आर्थिक वर्ष २०८२-८३ को जेठ मसान्तसम्म नौ हजार २४२ पर्यटकले आरक्ष भ्रमण गरिसकेका छन्। साउनमा ४९६, भदौमा ५४७, असोजमा ३२५, कात्तिकमा ५९१, मङ्सिरमा एक हजार ८९३, पुसमा ६४२, माघमा एक हजार ४९९, फागुनमा ६९७, चैतमा ६९१, वैशाखमा ७९१ र जेठमा एक हजार ७० पर्यटकले आरक्ष अवलोकन गरेका छन्।

सप्तकोशी नदीको बहावसँगै फैलिएको हरियाली, दुर्लभ अर्नाको बथान, चराचुरुङ्गीको चहलपहल र जलचरको जीवन्त उपस्थितिले कोशी टप्पुलाई जैविक विविधताको अनुपम आश्रयस्थलका रूपमा स्थापित गरेको छ। जैविक विविधताको दृष्टिले नेपालकै महत्वपूर्ण संरक्षित क्षेत्रमध्ये एक मानिने यन संरक्षणसँगै पर्यटन प्रवर्द्धनको ठूलो सम्भावना समेत रहेको छ।

सन् १९७६ को गणनामा कोशी टप्पुमा ६३ वटा अर्ना रहेका थिए भने सन् २०२१ को गणनाअनुसार सङ्ख्या बढेर चार सय ९८ पुगेको कोशी टप्पु बन्यजन्तु आरक्षका रेन्जर पौडेलले बताए। कोशी टप्पुमा ४२ प्रजातिका स्तनधारी, ५३५ प्रजातिका पन्छी, १४१ प्रजातिका माछा र ७७ प्रजातिका पुतली पाइन्छन्। विसं २०८० को गणनाअनुसार ३२ वटा खरमयुर तथा २०७९ को गणनाअनुसार १९ वटा डल्फिन अभिलेख गरिएको छ।

कोशी टप्पुमा विशेषगरी साइबेरिया,चीन, मङ्गोलिया र मध्य एसियाबाट जाडो छल्न आउने प्रवासी चराहरूको ठूलो सङ्ख्या देखिन्छ। चराविज्ञ अनिस तिमल्सिनाका अनुसार कोशी टप्पु उत्तरी गोलाद्र्धबाट आउने चराहरूको प्रमुख विश्रामस्थल हो। यदि चराहरूले विमानस्थल बनाउने हो भने नेपालमा उनीहरूको अन्तरराष्ट्रिय विमानस्थल कोशी टप्पु नै हुन्थ्यो। उनले भने, हिउँदयाम सुरु भएपछि चराहरू यन केही महिना बिताएर गर्मी सुरु हुनासाथ आफ्नै गन्तव्यतर्फ फर्कन्छन्।

कोशी टप्पुको अर्को प्रमुख आकर्षण नेपालमा प्राकृतिक रूपमा पाइने एकमात्र जङ्गली भैँसी (अर्ना) को मुख्य बासस्थान हुनु हो। आरक्षका विशाल घाँसे मैदान अर्नाका लागि उपयुक्त आवास मानिन्छन्। घाँस चरिदिने, बीउ फैलाउने र खुला चरन क्षेत्रको संरक्षणमा अर्नाले महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका खेल्ने संरक्षणकर्मीहरू बताउँछन्।

जङ्गली हात्ती, एकसिङ्गे गैँडा, निलगाई, चितल, रतुवा, लगुना, मलाह बिरालो, घडियाल, मगरगोही, अजिङ्गर, सुनगोहोरोलगायतका दुर्लभ प्रजाति पनि पाइन्छन्। यस जैविक सम्पदाले कोशी टप्पुलाई अनुसन्धान, अध्ययन र प्रकृति पर्यटनका लागि विशिष्ट केन्द्र बनाएको छ।

दुर्लभ अर्ना, प्रवासी चराचुरुङ्गी, जलचर र हरियालीले सजिएको कोशी टप्पु संरक्षण र पर्यटनलाई सँगसँगै अघि बढाउने नेपालको महत्वपूर्ण प्राकृतिक सम्पदाका रूपमा स्थापित हुँदै गएको छ। आरक्षको वनस्पति विविधता पनि उत्तिकै समृद्ध छ। यहाँ सिसौँ, खयर, सेमल, कदम्ब, साज र बाँसलगायत नदी किनारका वन तथा विशाल घाँसे मैदान पाइन्छन्।यिनै घाँसे मैदान अर्ना, हरिण र नीलगाईजस्ता वन्यजन्तुको मुख्य आश्रयस्थल मानिन्छन्।

स्थानीयका अनुसार कोशी टप्पुको जैविक विविधता, नदी प्रणाली, दुर्लभ वन्यजन्तु र स्थानीय संस्कृति नै यसको सबैभन्दा ठूलो सम्पत्ति हो। यी सम्भावनालाई योजनाबद्ध रूपमा पर्यटन उत्पादनमा रूपान्तरण गर्न पूर्वाधार विकास, प्रभावकारी प्रचारप्रसार र संरक्षणलाई सँगसँगै अघि बढाउन आवश्यक रहेको स्थानीयको भनाइ छ।

इटहरीबाट साथीहरूसँग घुम्न आएकी सरिता श्रेष्ठले कोशी टप्पुको प्राकृतिक सौन्दर्य, चराचुरुङ्गी अवलोकन तथा हात्ती र अर्ना हेर्ने अवसर विशेष आकर्षण भएको बताइन्। फुर्सदको समयमा हामी प्रायः यहाँ साथीहरुसँग आउने गर्छौं उनले भनिन्।

स्थानीय होटल व्यवसायी लोकबहादुर मगरका अनुसार कोशी टप्पुको पर्यटन विकास अझै प्रारम्भिक चरणमै छ। सीमित आवास सुविधा, कमजोर सडक पहुँच, अन्य पर्यटकीय पूर्वाधारको अभाव, प्रभावकारी प्रचारप्रसार नहुनु र पर्याप्त लगानीको कमीका कारण आरक्षको वास्तविक पर्यटन सम्भावनाको पूर्ण उपयोग हुन सकेको छैन।

उनका अनुसार कोशी टप्पुमा जङ्गल सफारी, प्रकृति पदयात्रा र स्थानीय संस्कृति अनुभव गर्ने गतिविधिप्रति पर्यटकको रुचि बढ्दै गएको छ। परिवारसँग बसेर ग्रामीण जीवनशैली, परम्परागत खानपान र संस्कृतिको अनुभव गर्न सकिने भएकाले कोशी टप्पु आसपासमा व्यवस्थित होमस्टेहरु विस्तार गर्नसके पर्यटक आगमन अझ बढ्न सक्ने उनको भनाइ छ। रासस

articles.title: Rolpa landslide update: Death toll rises to three in Rolpa landslide, nine still missing
articles.summary:
The death toll from a landslide in Rolpa has risen to three, with nine people still missing after heavy rain sent a torrent of mud and debris down a hillside in Thabang Rural Municipality-5 on Wednesday night.

The landslide struck Kotlabara at around 8:40 pm, burying houses, shops and cattle sheds where about seven families lived. Two people were seriously injured and rescued from the debris.

The latest death was that of 71-year-old Manarkhi Pun Magar, whose body was recovered from the debris on Thursday. The other victims were 18-year-old Shanti Pun Magar and 60-year-old Kamal Bahadur Pun Magar, according to the Lumbini Province Police Office.

The nine people still missing have been identified as 40-year-old Jun Kumari Pun Magar, nine-year-old Ashim Pun Magar, six-year-old Ashok Pun Magar, 75-year-old Dal Bahadur Pun Magar, 80-year-old Ajambar Pun Magar, 78-year-old Bal Bahadur Pun Magar, 72-year-old Lil Bahadur Pun Magar, 71-year-old Mani Pun Magar and 67-year-old Hastakala Roka Magar.

The injured, 22-year-old Himal Pun Magar and 25-year-old Sanjay Gharti Magar, were pulled from the debris by police and local residents and taken towards Sulaichaur for treatment.

The Area Police Office in Uwa was alerted at around 9:30 pm. A police team reached the site at about 10:15 pm and continued the search through the night. Rescue efforts resumed early Thursday as security personnel and residents worked to clear debris and locate those still missing.

Local health worker Bimarsh Gharti Magar said the steep and difficult terrain was hampering rescue efforts and making it difficult to reach the injured and those believed to be trapped.

Deputy Superintendent of Police Pancha Kumar Bakhu, Rolpa police chief, said the search and rescue operation was continuing and that more details would become available as rescuers made progress.

The landslide struck an area about 80 kilometres northeast of Liwang, the district headquarters. The Uwa area is considered highly vulnerable to landslides. A landslide in a nearby village several years ago killed at least six people.

The story has been updated.

articles.title: Landslide disrupts Bhotekoshi’s flow, downstream residents warned
articles.summary:
A large landslide near Nyalam on the Chinese side of the border has disrupted the flow of the Bhotekoshi river, prompting authorities to warn residents downstream to remain alert.

The landslide began falling from a cliff near Nyalam at around 6:30 am on Thursday, carrying rocks and earth into the river. The affected area lies on the Chinese side, across from the Bailey bridge connecting Liping Bazar, according to the Armed Police Force deployed along the border.

Kumar Shrestha, ward chairman of Bhotekoshi Rural Municipality-2, said part of the river had been obstructed by the debris, raising concerns that its flow could change suddenly and pose a risk to communities downstream.

“A landslide has been falling from the cliff around Jhimmu Post in Nyalam on the Chinese side since about 6:30 am Thursday,” Shrestha said. “As the landslide has affected the river’s flow, we have urged people downstream to remain alert.”

The District Police Office in Sindhupalchok said the Nepal Police and Armed Police Force were monitoring the river after the debris fell into it. Authorities have warned that further landslides could block the river, allowing water to accumulate and potentially triggering a sudden surge downstream.

Residents around the dam site, Jholunge, Lamosanghu, Khadichaur, Andheri, Kothe and Balephi Bazar in Balephi Rural Municipality have been specifically urged to exercise heightened caution.

However, Shashidhar Ghimire, chief district officer of Sindhupalchok, said reports that half of the river had been blocked were inaccurate. Only a small amount of debris had fallen into the river, and the Bhotekoshi river was continuing to flow normally, he said.

“Half of the river has not been blocked. Only a small amount of debris has fallen into the river, and the river is continuing to flow normally,” Ghimire said. “There is no need to panic at this point.”

Security agencies and local authorities are continuously monitoring the landslide site and the condition of the river, Ghimire said.

Residents have been advised to stay away from the riverbanks and downstream areas, remain in safe locations and move to higher or safer ground immediately if they notice any sudden change in the river’s flow.

articles.title: Police raid journalist Kishor Shrestha’s office after arrest
articles.summary:
Police raided the office of journalist Kishor Shrestha on Thursday morning, hours after arresting him at his home.

Shrestha is being held at the Kathmandu District Police Range and is due to be presented before a court on Thursday. Police said he was arrested for investigation on suspicion of violating Nepal’s Privacy Act, 2018.

A team from the Kathmandu District Police Range raided the office of Jana Aastha Saptahik in Jhamsikhel, Lalitpur, and seized computers, including CPUs and monitors, as well as other electronic devices.

Police spokesperson Superintendent of Police Dan Bahadur Thapa said the equipment was taken into custody as part of the investigation.

Journalists staged a protest outside the Kathmandu District Police Range on Thursday, demanding Shrestha’s immediate release. The demonstration was organised by the Federation of Nepali Journalists (FNJ), which has condemned his arrest and called for his unconditional release.

In a statement signed by FNJ general secretary Ram Prasad Dahal, the federation urged the authorities to end what it described as “anti-press” conduct, release Shrestha unconditionally and respect press freedom. It also said that any dispute over the content of a news report should be addressed through the appropriate process at the Press Council Nepal.

The federation said it had received information that, shortly after Shrestha’s arrest, police searched his home at around 1 am on Thursday, allegedly in an attempt to identify the source of the news report. Police also raided his office early Thursday morning, the FNJ said.
